item.title: Saudi Arabia’s PIF looking to sell 25% of Newcastle through share issue
item.description: PIF seeking investment to fund infrastructure projects JP Morgan appointed to handle the sale Newcastle United’s owner, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), is looking to sell up to 25% of the club by issuing new shares. The New York-based bank JP Morgan, whose most recent involvement in a major football deal was Fifa’s aborted attempt to sell off 20% of its commercial rights last summer, has been appointed to handle the sale, as first reported by the Athletic . Continue reading...

item.title: David Adelman Doesn’t Hold Back With Damning Message After Nuggets’ 19-Point Loss to Mavs
item.description: Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray After Loss to the Mavericks © X/@Nuggets Denver Nuggets head coach David Adelman put his team on blast after they were thoroughly defeated 120-101 by the Dallas Mavericks at home in NBA Cup action. The Nuggets went down 58-39 against Dallas, recording their lowest first-half scoring mark of the season. They responded with a 38-26 third quarter to offer a glimmer of hope to those who stayed up late to watch Tuesday’s game. However, Denver struggled to generate high-danger looks and rarely threatened Dallas down the stretch as they fell to 10-6 overall and 4-4 at home. Following the defeat, Adelman spoke to the media and voiced his displeasure in a manner rarely seen from him this season. “We were really lazy, the way we passed the ball,” Adelman said via @guerillasports on X. “Felt like I wanted to go back and coach a middle school camp about ball faking and not throwing it straight to people’s hands… we were not a good basketball team tonight.” Adelman has been patient with the team’s early-season struggles, but that approach may be changing. Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic Don’t Make Excuses After Nuggets Loss Nuggets stars Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic also fell well below their usual standards in the game, echoing their head coach’s frustration with the team’s poor execution after the loss. “It doesn’t matter what question you ask, honestly. We were just bad…sloppy, lazy,” Murray said . Murray finished with 20 points, two rebounds, and three assists but struggled with his shooting, going 6-of-17 from the field and 2-of-8 from beyond the arc. Jokic, meanwhile, had 18 points but also struggled with his efficiency, going 6-of-14 from the field and 1-of-4 from deep. He also recorded a team-high five turnovers. “We didn’t shoot the ball well, we didn’t finish well, we had a lot of turnovers,” Jokic said . The game highlighted some of the problems the Nuggets have faced on occasion this season. When Denver fails to score efficiently or create opportunities in transition, it struggles to open up the offense. It becomes much harder for Jokic and Murray when an opponent pushes the pace and attacks the paint the way Dallas did, forcing Denver into rushed shots and turnovers before its offense can get set. The Nuggets have put together a solid start at 10–6, and no team is perfect, but they still have a lot to learn and add if they want to make another deep playoff run. They now face a six-game road trip, beginning with a Friday matchup against the Utah Jazz (3-16), before returning home. item.title: Braves Need To Sign Jazz Chisholm Jr. In Free Agency
item.description: Free agent second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. Outside of signing Evan Phillips, the Atlanta Braves have been quiet in free agency. The Braves could use help in the outfield and rotation, and they also need a shortstop. Mauricio Dubón saved the team at shortstop last season, but he was also used in left field. Regardless, he is a free agent and the Braves need to make a move to replace his production and have some clarity in the infield. One option the Braves need to consider is Jazz Chisholm Jr. He did not have a good year in 2025, but he is a two-time All-Star and is one season removed from being a 30-30 player. Chisholm cost himself some money with his down year, but he could still end up finding a decent deal in free agency. There is reportedly tons of interest in him, and the Braves would be a good fit. He could slot in as the regular shortstop, or the Braves could use him at second base and make Ozzie Albies the shortstop. Even in a down year, Chisholm hit 19 home runs and stole 41 bases. He would be a massive upgrade from where the Braves were last offseason, thinking Ha-Seong Kim would be their regular shortstop. Adding Chisholm would not fix all of the Braves' issues. They would still need to add some pitching and a bat to play in left field. More MLB: Tarik Skubal's Dad Reveals Why Son Chose Mets Over Proven Winners

item.title: “The stadium is unbelievable” – Michael Ball weighs in on Everton’s commercial opportunities
item.description: LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 12: A general view of Hill Dickinson Stadium on November 12, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Tony McArdle/Everton FC via Getty Images) | Everton FC via Getty Images This article brought to you courtesy of betTOM . In a recent exclusive interview, Royal Blue Mersey were able to speak with former Evertonian Michael Ball on a variety of topics. Hill Dickinson Stadium and Everton’s identity Geoff: What do you think of Everton’s new stadium, and how could the club make more of it commercially? Michael Ball: “The stadium is unbelievable. You go there and it still has not quite sunk in that it is ours. Inside and out, it is fantastic. “I expected the Friedkin Group to take the commercial side to another level. That is no disrespect to Hill Dickinson, who stepped up as stadium sponsors, but I thought there might have been a bigger commercial deal. “They have tried different events and I would expect more concerts, but I would also like to see more Everton identity inside and outside the ground. “I don’t accept the argument that you cannot put branding on the seats because of concerts. When a concert is full, you cannot see the seats anyway. “There were always going to be a few teething problems, but supporters are enjoying it. Winning football matches is the most important thing, of course, but I would like visitors looking across the river to know immediately that it is Everton’s stadium.” What Everton need from new owners Geoff: Should Everton’s next owners be supporters at heart, or is investment the priority? Michael Ball: “You need a balance. “We have had owners with money and spent it badly. We have also had Evertonians involved who wanted the best for the club but could not deliver everything they hoped to achieve. “You want people who understand Everton, what the club means and what supporters expect, alongside people with the business knowledge and resources to move it forward. “The Friedkin Group have helped stabilise the club financially, and David Moyes has improved things on the pitch. They deserve credit for that. The disappointment is that they do not seem to want to take the next step. “The financial rules make it difficult to break consistently into the European places, so this will not be a quick process. But supporters want to see progress. “There are huge commercial opportunities now the stadium is built. In the past, I don’t think we fully capitalised on having Tim Howard in America or Tim Cahill in Australia. “The next ownership needs to understand the football club while also improving how Everton market themselves around the world.” Our thanks again to betTOM who facilitated the Zoom call with Michael Ball.

item.title: Today in White Sox History: November 25
item.description: On this day 75 years ago, Bucky Dent was born. | (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) 1951 Mid-1970s South Side shortstop Bucky Dent was born, in Savannah, Ga. He was a first round pick (No. 6 overall) of the White Sox in 1970, scooting to the majors by 1973 and finishing 1974 as the AL Rookie of the Year runner-up. Ultimately, his time in Chicago was underwhelming, with Dent distinguishing himself as a solid fielder and great bunter. After a terrible 1976 season, during which he practically talked himself out of Chicago, Bill Veeck gave Dent his wish, on the cusp of the 1977 season: A swap to New York for a package that included $200,000, slugger Oscar Gamble and future Cy Young winner LaMarr Hoyt . Dent blossomed into a star in New York, honing his fielding to an elite level, but Gamble was a 3.6 WAR value for the South Side Hit Men and Hoyt would provide 11.2 WAR over six seasons on the South Side — a package outpacing the 12.5 WAR that the feisty shortstop delivered to the Yankees. 1985 Ozzie Guillén of the White Sox was named AL Rookie of the Year by the Baseball Writers Association of America. Guillén, who came to the Sox in a deal involving 1983 Cy Young winner LaMarr Hoyt , didn’t disappoint. Offensively, Ozzie recorded 134 hits and had a .273 batting average. But it was his defense — carrying on a line of White Sox glove wizards from Venezuela — that was outstanding. In 150 games, Guillén only committed 12 errors the entire season and racked up 1.8 defensive WAR. It was the start of run through 1990 where the shortstop totaled 17.1 dWAR and ended with a 1990 Gold Glove — the only one of his 16-season career. He received 16 of 28 first-place votes, and finished with 101 points. Teddy Higuera of the Brewers was second. Ozzie returned as manager after his playing days ended. Twenty years after his ROY honors, Guillén piloted the White Sox to a 2005 World Series win. Also on this day, and perhaps not coincidentally, the White Sox traded shortstop Scott Fletcher , pitcher Ed Correa and a player to be named later (José Mota) to the Texas Rangers for pitcher Dave Schmidt and infielder Wayne Tolleson . Fletcher was excellent in his three remaining years of team control, manning shortstop regularly for the Rangers and amassing 11.9 WAR in that time. Schmidt was strong for the Sox in 1986 (1.7 WAR in relief, including closing duty that yielded eight saves) as was Tolleson (1.1 WAR in part-time play). But this was a bad trade overall for the White Sox, who would have been better served shifting Fletcher to second or third base instead of starting Julio Cruz or Tim Hulett . 2005 White Sox GM Ken Williams rolled the dice and traded popular center fielder Aaron Rowand to the Phillies for slugger Jim Thome . item.content:encoded: On this day 75 years ago, Bucky Dent was born. | (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) 1951 Mid-1970s South Side shortstop Bucky Dent was born, in Savannah, Ga. He was a first round pick (No. 6 overall) of the White Sox in 1970, scooting to the majors by 1973 and finishing 1974 as the AL Rookie of the Year runner-up. Ultimately, his time in Chicago was underwhelming, with Dent distinguishing himself as a solid fielder and great bunter. After a terrible 1976 season, during which he practically talked himself out of Chicago, Bill Veeck gave Dent his wish, on the cusp of the 1977 season: A swap to New York for a package that included $200,000, slugger Oscar Gamble and future Cy Young winner LaMarr Hoyt . Guillén, who came to the Sox in a deal involving 1983 Cy Young winner LaMarr Hoyt , didn’t disappoint. Offensively, Ozzie recorded 134 hits and had a .273 batting average. But it was his defense — carrying on a line of White Sox glove wizards from Venezuela — that was outstanding. In 150 games, Guillén only committed 12 errors the entire season and racked up 1.8 defensive WAR. It was the start of run through 1990 where the shortstop totaled 17.1 dWAR and ended with a 1990 Gold Glove — the only one of his 16-season career. He received 16 of 28 first-place votes, and finished with 101 points. Teddy Higuera of the Brewers was second. Ozzie returned as manager after his playing days ended. Twenty years after his ROY honors, Guillén piloted the White Sox to a 2005 World Series win. Also on this day, and perhaps not coincidentally, the White Sox traded shortstop Scott Fletcher , pitcher Ed Correa and a player to be named later (José Mota) to the Texas Rangers for pitcher Dave Schmidt and infielder Wayne Tolleson . Fletcher was excellent in his three remaining years of team control, manning shortstop regularly for the Rangers and amassing 11.9 WAR in that time. Schmidt was strong for the Sox in 1986 (1.7 WAR in relief, including closing duty that yielded eight saves) as was Tolleson (1.1 WAR in part-time play). But this was a bad trade overall for the White Sox, who would have been better served shifting Fletcher to second or third base instead of starting Julio Cruz or Tim Hulett . 2005 White Sox GM Ken Williams rolled the dice and traded popular center fielder Aaron Rowand to the Phillies for slugger Jim Thome . The Peoria native hammered 42 home runs and took the AL Comeback Player of the Year in 2006, but many felt the trade changed the chemistry and philosophy of the club that won the World Series in 2005 — to say nothing of the defensive hole it created in center field. Thome would play almost four years with the Sox and hit 134 home runs, along with three seasons of at least 90 RBIs. He hit his 500th career home run in 2007 at U.S. Cellular Field, beating the Angels with a walk-off blast. In addition to cash coming back to the White Sox along with Thome (making more than $14 million per year), two minor-leaguers were sent to Philadelphia, Daniel Haigwood and 20-year-old future starter standout Gio González . 2014 In a bold commitment to the designated hitter spot, the White Sox signed Adam LaRoche to a two-year, $25 million deal. After a 2012 season that saw LaRoche put up phenomenal production (33 homers, 100 RBIs, 127 OPS+, 4.2 WAR, sixth in NL MVP voting, Gold Glove, Silver Slugger), LaRoche fizzled om 2013 and rebounded in 2014. He seemed a safe, and left-handed, bat. However, things played out much uglier, as LaRoche faltered badly with his new team (12 homers and 44 RBIs in 127 games, 78 OPS+, -0.7 WAR). And during the next spring training, in one of the strangest stories ever to come out of the South Side, LaRoche abruptly retired after GM Ken Williams asked him to keep his son, Drake, out of the White Sox locker room; LaRoche walked away from his full $13 million salary for 2016 with the decision.

item.title: Should Raiders extend Tre Tucker or let him hit free agency?
item.description: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images We love getting our community members involved in our coverage whenever possible and this recent Feed post will serve as a great jumping off point on a topic: Indeed, Las Vegas Raiders starting wide receiver Tre Tucker is a pending free agent. Because of his speed and big-play potential, the Raiders’ 2023 third-round pick will likely have a solid market if he hits free agency. That Spotrac projection is probably in the correct range of what Tucker’s market will be. Remember, the Raiders signed wide receiver Jalen Nailor from the Minnesota Vikings this year to a three-year, $35.5 million deal. He had less starting experience than Tucker and he had produced less than tucker this season, so Tucker will surely be looking for a bigger per year average than Nailor received. The question is whether the Raiders should commit this type of deal to Tucker. They didn’t trade before the recent trade deadline, so they clearly like him. The Raiders don’t have a whole lot at wide receiver and will likely draft a player at the position regardless Tucker stays or goes. Another factor is that while Tucker has had his share of big plays, he hasn’t consistently made a big impact. So, in the end, do you think Tucker is worth this type of long-term commitment? item.title: 'Nothing's bigger than the NFL': Robert Griffin III pitches himself for promotion
item.description: Credit: Awful Announcing Podcast; NFL on Fox The domino effect of Troy Aikman potentially leaving ESPN could be significant, and it could start under Aikman’s original broadcasting roof at Fox Sports. Many presume ESPN will target Fox’s Greg Olsen to replace Aikman if the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback departs, leaving Olsen’s prestigious No. 2 spot open. Olsen has made news for years about his desire to return to calling top games after briefly doing so during Aikman and Tom Brady’s runs at Fox, but he continues to call premier matchups each Sunday and postseason games each winter. Currently, Drew Brees is the No. 3 NFL game analyst at Fox and would be the likely call-up to take Olsen’s spot if those initial dominoes fell. Brees recently pitched himself as a candidate to leap all the way to Monday Night Football , but that is unlikely. The more urgent matter for Brees is staving off competition to replace Olsen. That competition could come from Robert Griffin III, the versatile commentator currently working in Fox’s No. 2 college football booth alongside Connor Onion . Before joining Fox, the former Heisman Trophy winner worked the Monday Night Countdown desk at ESPN, hosts a fairly prominent podcast, and is outspoken on social media. In a recent appearance on The Awful Announcing Podcast , Griffin said he would be interested in Olsen’s role if he left. “Obviously the elephant in the media room right now is what’s going on with Troy at ESPN, and … you hear the rumors about Greg, maybe it’s Travis Kelce, maybe it’s whatever,” Griffin said. “I believe that you can call college games and you can call NFL games. I know Kirk Herbstreit is doing that right now with ESPN and at Amazon. But if Fox was to dub, ‘We want you guys to do NFL,’ that’s certainly something that I would consider. It’s fun, you know, and nothing’s bigger than the NFL.” During his media career so far, Griffin has made more of a name for himself in internet feuds and provocative takes than in breaking down games. But at Fox, Griffin often gets strong assignments because the network assigns its top announcing team to the noon game most weeks. Griffin has worked alongside talented play-by-play voices including Onion and Jason Benetti, and as he shared on the AA Podcast , cut back on some of the flashy elements of his broadcasting persona. While Griffin is right that some, like Herbstreit, call both NFL and college football, most do not. Nobody currently working at Fox Sports calls both levels of football. Is Griffin at a tier where the network would grant him that level of work? A lot has to happen before we find out. When asked if he had shared his aspirations directly with Fox execs, Griffin said simply: “Yes.” In the meantime, Griffin has his hands full interviewing to be Baylor’s next head football coach . The post Robert Griffin III has shared with Fox Sports that he wants to call NFL games appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Why Tiger Woods Is Building A Shadow Creek-Inspired Golf Oasis In Cabo
item.description: Diamante owner Ken Jowdy (left) with Tiger Woods (right), who is building a third golf course at the Cabo coastal community that's part of a new private club called Legacy. Diamante Cabo San Lucas Diamante built its reputation on golf, as the private coastline community in Cabo San Lucas jumped onto the global stage in 2010 with the Top 100-rated Dunes course and then added the first completed design from Tiger Woods in 2014. Now, after spending the past decade-plus adding amenities – many of them for non-golfers as it continued to grow -- Diamante is introducing a private club within the 1,500-acre community. And with it, another golf course from Woods and his TGR Design team. The Legacy Club is the final key piece in the land plans owner Ken Jowdy had sketched out for Diamante decades ago. Jowdy recently pulled out a land plan from 2005 – the year before he bought the pioneering property on the Pacific coast – and noted the three 18-hole golf courses he hoped to build sat in the same spots they occupy today. “Golf is still at our core for why people come here,” Jowdy said during an interview the week that Woods’ El Cardonal Course at Diamante hosted the PGA Tour’s recent World Wide Technology Championship. “We wanted to create something completely different than those other two (courses), and so that’s where the idea for the Legacy Course was born.” The new Tiger Woods-designed Legacy course, as seen during a recent tour of the property. Grow-in and construction is still continuing on the course, which is expected to open to members in November of 2027. Erik Matuszewski The centerpiece to the Legacy Club, and Diamante’s premier real estate offering, is a layout conceived as an “oasis in the desert” that’s drastically different than the other two championship courses on property. And from anything else in Cabo, for that matter. Jowdy’s inspiration for the Legacy course is the ultra-exclusive Shadow Creek in Las Vegas, a luxurious and perfectly manicured layout he calls one of his “favorite places on the planet.” Shadow Creek continues to be the benchmark for manufactured beauty in the golf world, created amid nothingness in the Nevada desert, and Legacy is similarly transforming the open desert landscape of southern Baja into a lush and secluded environment. “I would never be arrogant enough to think that this could ever compete with Shadow Creek, but you’ll see a lot of the inspiration,” said Jowdy, who won the Monday pro-am at Diamante during tournament week as part of a team with longtime friend Roger Clemens. “If we helicopter you in the middle of Shadow Creek, you don’t think you’re in Vegas. Here, you won’t think you’re in Cabo.” Legacy’s Difference A view of the Legacy Course from the Outpost, a dedicated on-course hospitality, activity and event hub within the private club. Erik Matuszewski Jowdy, the CEO and founder of Diamante Cabo San Lucas and Legacy Properties LLC, describes the Dunes course as a links-style layout while El Cardonal
item.content:encoded: Diamante owner Ken Jowdy (left) with Tiger Woods (right), who is building a third golf course at the Cabo coastal community that's part of a new private club called Legacy. Diamante Cabo San Lucas Diamante built its reputation on golf, as the private coastline community in Cabo San Lucas jumped onto the global stage in 2010 with the Top 100-rated Dunes course and then added the first completed design from Tiger Woods in 2014. Now, after spending the past decade-plus adding amenities – many of them for non-golfers as it continued to grow -- Diamante is introducing a private club within the 1,500-acre community. And with it, another golf course from Woods and his TGR Design team. The Legacy Club is the final key piece in the land plans owner Ken Jowdy had sketched out for Diamante decades ago. Jowdy recently pulled out a land plan from 2005 – the year before he bought the pioneering property on the Pacific coast – and noted the three 18-hole golf courses he hoped to build sat in the same spots they occupy today. “Golf is still at our core for why people come here,” Jowdy said during an interview the week that Woods’ El Cardonal Course at Diamante hosted the PGA Tour’s recent World Wide Technology Championship. “We wanted to create something completely different than those other two (courses), and so that’s where the idea for the Legacy Course was born.” The new Tiger Woods-designed Legacy course, as seen during a recent tour of the property. Grow-in and construction is still continuing on the course, which is expected to open to members in November of 2027. Erik Matuszewski The centerpiece to the Legacy Club, and Diamante’s premier real estate offering, is a layout conceived as an “oasis in the desert” that’s drastically different than the other two championship courses on property. And from anything else in Cabo, for that matter. Jowdy’s inspiration for the Legacy course is the ultra-exclusive Shadow Creek in Las Vegas, a luxurious and perfectly manicured layout he calls one of his “favorite places on the planet.” Shadow Creek continues to be the benchmark for manufactured beauty in the golf world, created amid nothingness in the Nevada desert, and Legacy is similarly transforming the open desert landscape of southern Baja into a lush and secluded environment. “I would never be arrogant enough to think that this could ever compete with Shadow Creek, but you’ll see a lot of the inspiration,” said Jowdy, who won the Monday pro-am at Diamante during tournament week as part of a team with longtime friend Roger Clemens. “If we helicopter you in the middle of Shadow Creek, you don’t think you’re in Vegas. Here, you won’t think you’re in Cabo.” Legacy’s Difference A view of the Legacy Course from the Outpost, a dedicated on-course hospitality, activity and event hub within the private club. Erik Matuszewski Jowdy, the CEO and founder of Diamante Cabo San Lucas and Legacy Properties LLC, describes the Dunes course as a links-style layout while El Cardonal is more “deserty,” like a lot of other courses in the Cabo area. Neither of those golf courses entailed the scope of work being done at Legacy. While about 200,000 cubic meters of dirt (and sand) was moved to build the Dunes, versus nearly 350,000 cubic meters at El Cardonal, Woods and his team moved over 3.5 million cubic meters at the new course. This earth-moving results in the course sitting down behind tall dunes – creating a private sanctuary hidden from other parts of the property – much of the dirt itself was moved to build up tiers of land upon which the club’s new custom homes, villas and condos are being constructed. The only houses directly on the course itself will be on the 14 lots for the Legacy founders, the first of which belongs to Woods himself. A site plan for the Legacy Club, with Founders home sites — including those for Woods and Jowdy — in the middle of the course routing. Diamante Cabo San Lucas A tour of the course provided a small taste of what’s to come, with five lakes spread throughout that are connected by a network of streams and are punctuated by multiple cascades and waterfalls. Beyond the water system, which alone cost $7 million, the abundance of plants, trees and flowers are taking root, and giant bags of brilliant white sand (like the kind found at Augusta National) are ready to be dumped into bunkers. “At the end of the day, I think the conditions are one thing that make a place great,” Jowdy said. “Not many people understand the nuances of a golf hole. But they’ll know when the course is in great condition. Course conditioning is something that trumps a lot of the nuances that 99% of people don’t get on what could be considered a great golf design. If the greens, fairways and bunkers are in great condition, that’s what people will take home.” Jowdy said he’s been fortunate to visit a good number of golf destinations during his travels and tries to “draw little things from those places” and put his spin on it as a consumer. Woods, similarly, is putting his spin on yet another golf course at Diamante, having not only built El Cardonal but also Oasis, the property’s 12-hole par-3 course. “He’s on top of the design. He knows everything that’s going on,” said Jowdy, who has the house next to Woods within the Legacy Club. The Tiger Connection Tiger Woods (left) and Diamante owner Ken Jowdy (right) during an early tour at the site of the forthcoming Woods-designed Legacy Course. Diamante Cabo San Lucas The two were introduced by a mutual friend about 15 years ago and met for the first time on Woods’ boat in Miami. Jowdy said he spent the first 20 to 30 minutes of that get-together talking with Woods’ then caddie, Joe LaCava, who he learned had attended a rival high school in Connecticut. The two played multiple sports against one another. And it was sports that created a bond with Woods, too. Especially when the group had been watching basketball in the living area and, upon dinner being served in the dining room, Woods pressed a button to flip the television around into that room. “As soon as that happened, I knew that we would get along well,” Jowdy said. “And then he was in on the vision when he saw the property,” Jowdy added. “We knew that his name was going to bring recognition here and we worked out a long-term deal. I think the best contracts are the ones you sign, put in the drawer and never look at again. This has been one of those.” Camilo Villegas plays a shot from a bunker at the Woods-designed El Cardonal course at Diamante during the PGA Tour's 2025 World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) Getty Images In addition to the Woods connection, the PGA Tour affiliation has brought further validation to the Diamante property. And Jowdy said he expects the new Legacy course will be ready for member play by late 2027 when the World Wide Technology Championship makes its return to the southern tip of Mexico. Meanwhile, homes and homesites continue to sell, with one founders’ lot at the other end of the row from Woods’ house priced at about $7.5 million. Ultimately, only 250 families within Diamante will have access to Legacy and the private golf and recreation club. “We have two great golf courses, but we needed a country club,” said Jowdy. “We needed a real club for the community. And that’s what Legacy is.” This article was originally published on Forbes.com

A lockout is set to take effect at the end of the day on Dec. 1, ending all transactions until the owners and players agree to a new collective bargaining agreement. As we saw five years ago, that will likely take some time. 2021 offers an indication of how offseason transactions could play out: there was a flurry of activity leading up to start of the lockout, but plenty of significant moves had to wait until after the lockout was lifted more than three months later. If reports are any indication, though, No. 1 free agent Tarik Skubal has a strong chance to sign before the lockout begins, raising the level of intrigue around free agency. The Sporting News is tracking the latest MLB rumors, signings and trades before the lockout begins. Follow along below with the latest news. The Royals are signing the third baseman on the heels of the Maikel Garcia trade to the Mariners, opening a spot in KC's corner infield. Cincinnati surprised many by not trading Stephenson at the deadline in August, but the decision makes more sense with a deal to bring back the team's serviceable starting catcher. Taylor was excellent against left-handed pitching with the Mets and Cubs in 2026 and plays solid defense, so he will at the very least be a valuable platoon player as he heads to the South Side. The Royals are signing the third baseman on the heels of the Maikel Garcia trade to the Mariners, opening a spot in KC's corner infield. The deal also includes a $5 million signing bonus for the right-handed pitcher. The Blue Jays missed out on Tarik Skubal, and pivot to the 27-year-old to pair with Dylan Cease in the rotation. Taira switched between the rotation and bullpen of the Seibu Lions over the last few season, but posted a 1.36 ERA as a full-time starter in 2026. Tigers add Ha-Seong Kim to infield Date : Nov. 24 Source : Jeff Passan The Tigers are adding infielder Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year, $5 million deal. Kim struggled mightily offensively with the Braves in 2026, batting a career-low .116 with a .216 OBP. Detroit is hoping that it's an anomaly and Kim can provide some depth in the infield. Orioles make massive move to sign Freddy Peralta Date : Nov. 24 Source : Ben Nicholson-Smith Freddy Peralta is cashing in. After reviving his season with the Rays in the back half of this year, the Orioles are bringing in the right-hander to headline their rotation. Peralta struggled to start 2026 with the Mets, but a trade to Tampa Bay worked wonders for him. He went 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA in 10 starts and was stellar in the Rays' run to the World Series, recording an astonishing 2.95 ERA in five appearances. Guardians bring in Kris Bubic Date : Nov. 24 Source : Jeff Passan The Guardians are adding to their pitching staff, signing lefty Kris Bubic on a one-year, $17.5 million deal. The 29-year-old split his time between the Royals and Dodgers last year, traded to L.A. at the deadline. He was limited to just nine starts and 14 appearances, posting a 3.76 ERA. Cubs land Japanese free agent Teruki Sato Date : Nov. 24 Source : Michael Cerami The top Japanese free agent of the 2026 offseason is heading to Chicago as the Cubs have reportedly agreed to a six-year, $120 million contract for the outfielder. The 27-year-old won the Triple Crown for the Hanshin Tigers this year and is a two-time Central League MVP. Sato is expected to play corner outfield, likely replacing free agent Seiya Suzuki. Cubs give Trevor Rogers 5-year deal Date : Nov. 24 Source : Jeff Passan The Cubs are bolstering their rotation, signing lefty Trevor Rogers to a five-year, $120 million contract. Rogers broke out with the Orioles in 2025, posting a 1.81 ERA and 9-3 record, but he regressed back to the norm this past year, going 10-11 with a 4.03 ERA. Chicago is hoping he finds his 2025 form again in the Windy City. Yankees sign reliever Brent Suter Date : Nov. 23 Source : Jeff Passan New York adds the 37-year-old Suter on a one-year deal worth $4 million as the Yankees aim to reshape their bullpen. Suter has been both a starter and reliever in his career, and he will start out the season in the Yankees' bullpen. Teruaki Sato could sign before Thanksgiving Date : Nov. 23 Source : Ken Rosenthal The Japanese star needs to sign before the pending lockout next week, and it seems like he is on track to sign somewhere this week. The Phillies, Blue Jays, Yankees and Mets are all teams that have been linked to the slugger. Mets add Paul Goldschmidt Date : Nov. 23 Source : Jon Heyman The veteran Goldshmidt isn't the star he used to be, but he can still defend at first base and hit lefties after serving as a platoon player with the Yankees. He will likely form a platoon with Jared Young at first base for the Mets next season. Tarik Skubal agrees to deal with Mets Date : Nov. 22 Source : J on Heyman The Mets have agreed to a nine-year, $450 million deal with Skubal, Jon Heyman and Jeff Passan report. Skubal's free agency ends more than a week before the lockout as the Mets make him by far the highest-paid pitcher in MLB history in terms of both total value and average annual value. Tigers add former Rookie of the Year Luis Gil Date : Nov. 22 Source : Jeff Passan The Tigers have agreed to a one-year, $2.3 million deal with non-tendered former Yankees starter Luis Gil. Gil was the AL Rookie of the Year in 2024 but has battled injuries and control issues over the last two seasons while also seeing his strikeout rate plummet. Jarren Duran drawing interest from several teams Date : Nov. 22 Source : Chris Cotillo, Sean McAdam Red Sox OF Jarren Duran remains a trade candidate despite being tendered a contract and is drawing interest from the Padres, Phillies and Mariners, MassLive reports. The Cubs were previously reported as another suitor for Duran. Ty France seeking 3-year deal Date : Nov. 21 Source : K en Rosenthal, Will Sammon Fresh off a resurgent season with the Padres, free-agent Ty France is reportedly seeking a three-year deal. The Athletic reports France is looking for an average annual salary between Jake Bauers' $14.5 million and Jorge Polanco's $20 million from last winter. Mets offered Skubal nine-year deal worth almost $400 million Date : Nov. 20 Source : Jim Duquette The Mets appear to be the most aggressive suitor for Skubal, with an initial offer that would allow Skubal to break multiple pitching contract records. Skubal also met with the Blue Jays, Dodgers and Padres thus far. Cubs claim catcher Joey Bart off waivers Date : Nov. 20 Source : Robert Murray The former No. 2 overall pick heads to the Cubs after he played for multiple teams in 2026. He should be a depth catcher option and could ultimately replace Carson Kelly, who is a free agent this offseason. Jonathan Loaisiga goes back to Yankees Date : Nov. 20 Source : Jorge Castillo It's a two-year deal for Loaisiga, with a club option for the 2029 season,

item.title: Men’s Basketball Recap: #13 St. John’s
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 24: Interim head coach Tony Stubblefield of the Oregon Ducks looks on against the St. John's Red Storm during the first half during the Players Era 16 bracket of The 2026 Players Era Men's Championship at Michelob ULTRA Arena on November 24, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Zach Del Bello/Players Era/Getty Images) | Getty Images Your Oregon Ducks took on #13 St. John’s on Tuesday night as part of the Players Era tournament in Las Vegas. The Ducks would keep it close through most of the first half, trailing by just 3 points at 25-22 with 7 minutes remaining. But St. John’s would go on a 20-8 run to close the half, and the Ducks would trail 45-30 at the break. The second half would start the way the first half ended, with St. John’s growing their lead steadily until it reached a game high 22 points with just under 10 minutes left in the ballgame, and it looked like that would be all she wrote for the Ducks. But then Oregon started to show some fight, using the next 7 minutes to trim the deficit down to just 8 points. But with only 1:40 remaining, the Ducks ran out of time, and they would wind up losing 90-79. Final in Las Vegas. #GoDucks pic.twitter.com/YdvKLRwmjl — Oregon Men's Basketball (@OregonMBB) November 25, 2026 Tonight we saw the clear difference between a national contender and a team looking to return to relevance. The St. John’s defense was SUFFOCATING at various times throughout the game, but especially after a made basket. Their full-court pressure had the Ducks in dire straits all game, forcing the Ducks into 15 turnovers. The shooting wasn’t there again either, with Oregon going just 3-15 from three. Hopefully they’ll be able to bounce back in their next matchup, on Thanksgiving night against (ugh) #5 Texas Tech. As always, ‘Sco Ducks

item.title: Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany not looking for handouts or sympathy vs. LOSC Lille
item.description: (Photo by Sven Hoppe/picture alliance via Getty Images) Bayern Munich are navigating a difficult stretch of injuries, missing significant attacking production and several key players heading into the Champions League clash with Lille. Vincent Kompany is not hiding from the reality of the situation, but he also is not interested in making excuses. The message from the Bayern coach is simple: the players available have to step up, find solutions, and prove themselves on the pitch. Kompany said the scale of the absences demands honesty, but also belief in the players who remain. “I think it’s important to always be realistic and honest, then start from the situation we’re in, find solutions and, eventually, start pushing forward and get results. What I mean by that is that I think we scored around 180 goals last year. About 130 of those goals are now gone. That’s a fact. That’s where you have to start. But what we do have is players who can run and fight. We have players who can step up in important moments. That helps rebuild belief, and we also have our fans behind us. So you go into a game like this with a lot of courage and determination, with a real desire to show that what we have right now is also Bayern. And, well, the only way to demonstrate that is on the pitch. I’m not going to do it here in a press conference. I hope we can show that [Wednesday],” Kompany said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). The return of some injured players could help Bayern rebuild their depth over the coming weeks, but Kompany stressed that nobody returning from injury should be expected to immediately carry the team. Kompany stated on whether Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz are ready to start and how he will handle players returning from injury: “Over the next two weeks, we hope to get Jamal [fully] fit again, get Lucho fit again and, hopefully, also Serge Gnabry and Alphonso Davies. Michael will also return at some point, hopefully sooner rather than later. So the outlook is that the team will be able to rebuild its strength quickly. Harry and Saibari will be out for longer, as you know, and so will Manu. But when it comes to reintegrating all these players returning from injury, I don’t want us to suddenly have the expectation that Lucho plays 20 minutes and has to score three goals. That’s not going to happen,” Kompany remarked. “The players who are fit have to perform and deliver results. Those returning from injury simply need to get back to full fitness as quickly as possible. Once they’re fit again, they will naturally become regular members of our team. So, regarding the question about Lucho: I’m delighted that he’s back, but [Wednesday]’s result cannot depend on Lucho. It has to depend on the other players.” Bayern’s second-half struggles against Köln exposed how difficult it can be to compensate for so many absences, particularly when players are forced into unfamiliar roles. item.content:encoded: (Photo by Sven Hoppe/picture alliance via Getty Images) Bayern Munich are navigating a difficult stretch of injuries, missing significant attacking production and several key players heading into the Champions League clash with Lille. Vincent Kompany is not hiding from the reality of the situation, but he also is not interested in making excuses. The message from the Bayern coach is simple: the players available have to step up, find solutions, and prove themselves on the pitch. Kompany said the scale of the absences demands honesty, but also belief in the players who remain. “I think it’s important to always be realistic and honest, then start from the situation we’re in, find solutions and, eventually, start pushing forward and get results. What I mean by that is that I think we scored around 180 goals last year. About 130 of those goals are now gone. That’s a fact. That’s where you have to start. But what we do have is players who can run and fight. We have players who can step up in important moments. That helps rebuild belief, and we also have our fans behind us. So you go into a game like this with a lot of courage and determination, with a real desire to show that what we have right now is also Bayern. And, well, the only way to demonstrate that is on the pitch. I’m not going to do it here in a press conference. I hope we can show that [Wednesday],” Kompany said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). The return of some injured players could help Bayern rebuild their depth over the coming weeks, but Kompany stressed that nobody returning from injury should be expected to immediately carry the team. Kompany stated on whether Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz are ready to start and how he will handle players returning from injury: “Over the next two weeks, we hope to get Jamal [fully] fit again, get Lucho fit again and, hopefully, also Serge Gnabry and Alphonso Davies. Michael will also return at some point, hopefully sooner rather than later. So the outlook is that the team will be able to rebuild its strength quickly. Harry and Saibari will be out for longer, as you know, and so will Manu. But when it comes to reintegrating all these players returning from injury, I don’t want us to suddenly have the expectation that Lucho plays 20 minutes and has to score three goals. That’s not going to happen,” Kompany remarked. “The players who are fit have to perform and deliver results. Those returning from injury simply need to get back to full fitness as quickly as possible. Once they’re fit again, they will naturally become regular members of our team. So, regarding the question about Lucho: I’m delighted that he’s back, but [Wednesday]’s result cannot depend on Lucho. It has to depend on the other players.” Bayern’s second-half struggles against Köln exposed how difficult it can be to compensate for so many absences, particularly when players are forced into unfamiliar roles. Kompany believes the team has spent the past few days addressing precisely that problem. Kompany said on how he is preparing Bayern’s attack amid the injuries: “In the second half against Köln, we simply noticed that many players were playing out of their usual positions. They perhaps weren’t familiar enough with the movements and combinations required in those positions, and that disrupted our rhythm even further,” Kompany said. “What we’ve hopefully managed to achieve, and this is my objective, is that since the day before yesterday, yesterday and today, we’ve been working quite extensively on the positions the players might occupy [Wednesday]. I don’t want to reveal anything just yet, but I hope we’ve developed the kind of understanding where we don’t have to think twice about every pass or movement. That’s what I felt was missing in the second half against Köln, and it disrupted our rhythm.” As for Lille, Kompany expects a side that will look to make life difficult for Bayern rather than sit back and absorb pressure. “They were still second in the French league last week. There’s always been a lot of talent at this club, which is very well known for its youth development. They have pace on the counter-attack and are definitely a team that presses aggressively and defends on the front foot. They’ve also made a few changes this season, and they have some experienced players who have been competing at international level for quite some time. But I think, playing at home, they’ll want to put on a positive performance for their fans. So I expect them to press high and deliver an entertaining game for the spectators overall,” said Kompany. With Harry Kane and Michael Olise unavailable, Bayern will inevitably look different, but Kompany believes the squad still has enough qualities to win. Kompany talked about what changes without Kane and Olise. “A lot. But I also don’t want to talk too much about the players who aren’t here. This is about the players we have available, and we can bring different things to this game. Not the same things, but different qualities,” Kompany stated. “We’ll have intensity, and we’ll have players who can decide a game. I believe that, and we have to maintain that belief.” The scrutiny surrounding Jamal Musiala has also been a talking point this week, but Kompany insists Bayern are keeping their focus within the team’s own bubble rather than getting caught up in the outside noise. “It’s natural that things aren’t completely calm. We’re human beings too. But we’re still very much in our own tunnel, in the bubble I’ve spoken about from the very beginning. And that’s exactly what helps us in moments like these. We’re focused on our next opponent and on what lies ahead of us [Wednesday]. I think that’s where you can best find your inner balance. I also understand that, when the opportunity presents itself, journalists sometimes use these situations as a topic. I understand that. But what shouldn’t be overlooked is how much experience and composure we have within this club,” said Kompany. “These situations are simply part of professional football for us. They’re part of being at a top club. We know how to deal with them. We have our own approach, and we’re staying calm and composed throughout the process. Ultimately, we know that everything will be decided on the pitch. In the meantime, you can’t explain everything. I can’t just come out and say this, that and the other. But I know that after the game, I’ll have more or fewer arguments to support our position. And that’s a mindset that is very much alive within our group. It gives us additional motivation.” Finally, Kompany was asked about the possibility of unconventional solutions, including playing Dayot Upamecano up front or turning to youngsters such as Bastian Assomo. While he is considering every option, the Bayern coach is determined not to panic. Kompany said on whether he considered Upamecano up front and whether youngsters like Assomo are options. “You can certainly come up with plenty of creative ideas, but there are other options as well. What I’m trying to do – and this is what I mean by staying calm – is make sure that we don’t suddenly start trying everything just because a particular idea comes to mind. We try to think carefully about what would suit the team, taking into account the formation, performances, playing time and what we’ve seen in the past. We discuss everything calmly, exchange our thoughts and then make decisions. And once those decisions are made, I stand behind them 100%. That’s also my responsibility. But I can assure you that we’re weighing up everything. Ultimately, we reach what we believe is the best decision, and usually quite quickly. Then I make the decisions and we move forward,” Kompany said. For Bayern Munich, the answers to all of these questions will have to come on the pitch. Kompany has made his position clear: no excuses, no panic, and no hiding from the challenge. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications sys

item.title: SEC Athletic Director Shoots Down Interest from University of Michigan
item.description: The University of Michigan’s search for its next athletic director continues to generate headlines, and apparently, another prominent SEC athletic director isn’t interested in making the move to Ann Arbor. According to a recent report, South Carolina athletic director Jeremiah Donati turned down an opportunity to interview for Michigan’s opening. The revelation is particularly interesting considering Michigan has since backed out of its agreement to hire Trev Alberts away from Texas A&M. The Wolverines now find themselves continuing their search for a permanent replacement for Warde Manuel , while facing considerable backlash from Michigan fans over the handling of the situation. Jeremiah Donati, University of South Carolina Athletics Director speaks with media during the South Carolina football’s Williams-Brice Stadium tour Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026 in Columbia, S.C. It is the latest progress in the first of South Carolina Athletics’ planned three-phased Williams-Brice Stadium Reimagined Project. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jeremiah Donati Turns Down Michigan’s Interest According to a report from Jordan Kaye of The State , two sources with knowledge of the situation confirmed that Donati recently declined a request to interview for Michigan’s athletic director position. Michigan retained search firm ZRG Turnkey to oversee its search, a firm South Carolina has previously utilized for several of its own hires. Donati arrived at South Carolina in December 2024 after spending 12 years at TCU, including seven as the Horned Frogs’ athletic director. According to the report, he currently earns $2 million annually and is under contract with the Gamecocks through June 30, 2031. Since arriving in Columbia, Donati has overseen increased investment in South Carolina’s athletic programs while helping advance renovations to Williams-Brice Stadium. His experience navigating the financial challenges of modern college athletics makes it understandable why Michigan would have expressed interest. Michigan’s Athletic Director Search Raises More Questions Michigan’s search has already taken an unexpected turn after the university reversed course on hiring Alberts, a development also covered by the Associated Press . Now, the revelation that another prominent SEC athletic director previously declined an interview adds another layer to the situation. It is important to note that Donati reportedly turned down Michigan’s interest before the Alberts agreement fell apart. There is no indication that Michigan has approached Donati again or that he has reconsidered his decision. For a university with Michigan’s resources, national brand, and athletic tradition, there should be no shortage of qualified candidates. However, between Donati declining an interview and the Alberts agreement falling apart, Michigan’s search certainly hasn’t gone according to plan.

item.title: 43, 269, 402: Willi Orbán’s week for the history books
item.description: 43, 269, 402: Willi Orbán’s week for the history books On Saturday, he drew level with Péter Gulácsi , on Tuesday, he overtook Yussuf Poulsen – and on Sunday, Willi Orbán could break another club record. More than eleven years into his RBL career , our number 4 is still breaking records. Willi could soon have made more appearances for RBL than anyone else in three different competitions , and he’s closing in on the club’s overall appearance record too. Could Willi overtake Péte in Freiburg? Willi made his 269th Bundesliga appearance for RB Leipzig in the 5-1 away win over 1. FC Union Berlin , drawing level with Péter Gulácsi , who had previously held the record outright. If Willi features against SC Freiburg on Sunday (15:30 CET) , he’ll have played more Bundesliga games for the Red Bulls than anyone else. Willi leads the way in the Champions League Willi is already out on his own in the Champions League . Our centre-back made his 43rd appearance in the competition for RBL in the 3-1 win over RC Lens , overtaking his long-time teammate Yussuf Poulsen . From our Champions League debut against AS Monaco in September 2017 to our latest victory over Lens, no other player has represented the Red Bulls on as many Champions League nights as Willi. Willi also holds the club record for DFB-Pokal appearances . He’s now played 38 games in the competition, four more than Yussi (34) , whose record he broke last season. Just 24 games away from the all-time club record Across all competitions , however, there’s still one player ahead of Willi: Yussuf Poulsen. Our former striker left Leipzig in the summer of 2025 after twelve years and 425 competitive appearances for the club. Willi has now made 402 appearances . Another 23 games would see him draw level with Yussi, while 24 would give him the record outright . If he continues to feature regularly, our centre-back could reach that milestone before the end of the season . Willi’s ability to keep performing at this level at the age of 34 is a testament to years of hard work. After making his 400th competitive appearance for RBL against FC Augsburg, he was asked about the secret to his fitness. “People are always looking for some magic formula , but it’s not as if I’m injecting myself with some miracle drug,” said Willi with a smile. “I just try to do my job properly and make sure I look after myself.” Micho: “It’s an honour to be his coach” When Willi joined Leipzig from 1. FC Kaiserslautern in the summer of 2015 , the Red Bulls were still playing in Bundesliga 2 . Since then, he’s played his part in our promotion to the Bundesliga, our run to the Champions League semi-finals, two DFB-Pokal triumphs and a Supercup win . He’s remained a mainstay of the team throughout, regardless of who’s been in charge. Martín Demichelis knows just how important Willi is to the team. item.description: Quinshon Judkins (RB21) and Ollie Gordon II (RB24) are my Week 12 fantasy football RB starts, as the Cleveland Browns host the Las Vegas Raiders and the Miami Dolphins host the New York Jets, the week’s two softest RB matchups. Zach Charbonnet (RB31) and Travis Etienne Jr. (RB32) are my sits. The Seattle Seahawks back visits a San Francisco 49ers defense allowing the third-fewest RB points since Week 7, and the New Orleans Saints back brings a thin receiving role to the Cincinnati Bengals. MORE: Week 12 fantasy football PPR rankings: Gibbs, Burrow lead as Walker nears return How did my Week 11 RB picks fare? Both starts finished as RB2s, and Tyler Allgeier finished outside the top 40. Aaron Jones Sr.’s touchdown pushed him into RB2 range, so last week’s calls went 3-1. Starts : David Montgomery (RB13 finish): 26 carries for 107 yards and 3 catches for 17 yards in the Houston Texans’ 26-3 win over the Indianapolis Colts. He came back from a four-game absence with a groin injury and set season highs in carries and rushing yards. Omarion Hampton (RB20 finish): 14 carries for 89 yards and 1 catch for 4 yards in the Los Angeles Chargers’ 27-24 loss to the Jets. His 36-yard run was his longest of the season, and he has 254 rushing yards over his last three games. Week 12: vs. Las Vegas, 28.7 FP/game to RBs in Weeks 7-11 (fourth) Week 10: vs. Houston, 10 car. for 38 yds, 1 TD, 3 rec. for 33 yds Judkins hasn’t given fantasy managers much to celebrate in his second season. The Ohio State product is averaging 3.4 yards per carry with four touchdowns in nine games, and he hasn’t reached 100 rushing yards in a game yet. The Raiders are the right opponent to change that. They’ve allowed 13 rushing touchdowns to backs this season, including 400 rushing yards and five scores over Weeks 9-11. The Raiders have also stuffed only 35.9% of opposing runs , which takes pressure off a Cleveland line that has struggled to open lanes. The game script should help too. Dylan Sampson outsnapped Judkins in Week 10 only because the Browns fell behind the Texans 17-0 before rallying. Cleveland is 4-0 at home. Las Vegas arrives with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza after a 38-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. If the Browns play from ahead, Judkins should get most of the carries against a defense that keeps giving backs chances to score. MORE: Week 12 fantasy football QB start-sit: Darnold, Mahomes, Watson, Williams Week 12 RB start ’em: Ollie Gordon II, Dolphins Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II (0) rushes the ball against the Indianapolis Colts | Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Week 12: vs. N.Y. Jets, 28.8 FP/game to RBs in Weeks 9-11 (second) Week 11: at Buffalo, 11 car. for 69 yds Gordon has been one of fantasy’s steadiest backs since taking over Miami’s backfield with De’Von Achane sidelined. The second-year back has at least 64 scrimmage yards in seven straight games, including 115 yards on 24 touches against the Colts in Week 10. His 11 carries in a 26-9 loss to the Buffalo Bills were his fewest since Week 4, but he still averaged 6.3 yards per carry. A four-game touchdown drought is the knock, and the Jets are the right team to end it. Gordon ran 25 times for 103 yards and a touchdown against New York in Week 7. Over Weeks 9-11, the Jets allowed 445 rushing yards and five total touchdowns to backs, and Hampton just ran for 89 yards on them. Coach Jeff Hafley has said Gordon “runs violent.” Quarterback Kyle McCord is still looking for a touchdown pass after two starts, so Miami has every reason to keep feeding the former Oklahoma State star. Coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that the former UCLA star is “probably playing some of his best football.” That 94-yard game came against a Raiders defense that ranks among the four most generous to backs in every window. San Francisco has been the opposite, allowing only 170 rushing yards, one rushing touchdown and 29 receiving yards to backs over Weeks 9-11. The 49ers then held Jordan Mason and Jones to 68 rushing yards on 19 carries in Mexico City. Charbonnet also didn’t catch a pass against Las Vegas, and rookie Jadarian Price took 10 touches. Without receiving work, Charbonnet needs a touchdown against one of the league’s stingiest run defenses to return flex value. That makes him a low-end RB3 this week. MORE: NFC power rankings Week 12 spotlight Bears-Lions as NFC North Thanksgiving headliner Week 12 RB sit ’em: Travis Etienne Jr., Saints New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne (3) runs on the field prior to the game against the Las Vegas Raiders | Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Week 12: at Cincinnati, 18.6 FP/game to RBs (21st) Week 11: at Chicago, 14 car. for 76 yds The former Clemson star took 14 of the Saints’ 16 running back carries against the Chicago Bears. But 46 of his 76 yards came on one run, the longest by a Saints running back since 2020 . His other 13 carries gained 30 yards, and he didn’t catch his only target. The bigger problem is passing downs. CJ Donaldson matched Etienne’s 32 snaps and caught four passes, and Alvin Kamara caught the Saints’ only touchdown. The Bengals have allowed 88.6 rushing yards per game and seven rushing touchdowns to backs in 10 games, so the run game doesn’t offer an easy matchup either. If the 3-7 Saints fall behind Joe Burrow and Cincinnati, Etienne could lose carries without the targets to make up for them. item.title: Five Washington Huskies for Ducks fans to know in Week 13
item.description: During the 2026 season, the Oregon Ducks have faced their share of injury-laden teams. If you include the injury to UCLA Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava mid-game, the Ducks have faced five backup quarterbacks this year. That won't be the case in the season-finale against the Washington Huskies , as they're just now regaining health and looking to be at full strength after downing the No. 8 Indiana Hoosiers in overtime last week. The Huskies have had an interesting season, as they began ranked No. 17 in the preseason AP poll and jumped out to a 3-0 start in non-conference play despite subpar offensive play. They then lost their next three games, falling to 3-3 and looking to be on verge of even making a bowl game. Since then, Washington has won four of five and gained tons of positive momentum going into their Week 13 trip to Eugene to take on the arch-rival Ducks. The normal characters are playing well for the Huskies: quarterback Demond Williams Jr. and safety Alex McLaughlin, but there are other stars playing well down the stretch for Washington. Here are five Huskies that Ducks fans should know, or get more familiar with how they're currently performing, before kickoff at Autzen Stadium on Saturday afternoon. QB Demond Williams Jr. One of the most dynamic quarterbacks in all of college football, it's been a bumpy year for Williams. He suffered a rib injury and was briefly the backup for one game before earning back his starting job over the last four games. Since then, he's played terrific football, perfectly meshing his creativity in the pass game with his excellence in the run game. Standing 5-foot-11 and 190 pounds, Williams manages to get out of tough situations and make extremely difficult plays look easy. At his worst, he can commit careless turnovers, but when Washington's on, he can dissect and run past any defense in the country. But he entered the transfer portal during the Ducks' CFP run to return home. He's missed six games due to a shoulder injury, but when he's healthy, he's a wrecking ball at 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, running through tacklers with ease. He leads the team with 78 tackles and has three interceptions, a forced fumble and eight passes defensed in 2026. The Chandler, AZ, native is rangy and uses his 6-foot-2, 205-pound frame to get all over the field, deployed near the line of scrimmage and on the back end of the defense. item.title: ‘If You’re Not Going to Play Me, Then Release Me’ — NFL Insider Predicts Aaron Rodgers’ Next Move After Steelers’ ‘Ultimate Indignity’
item.description: ‘If You’re Not Going to Play Me, Then Release Me’ — NFL Insider Predicts Aaron Rodgers’ Next Move After Steelers’ ‘Ultimate Indignity’ The football world was hit with a shocking update when the Pittsburgh Steelers announced that they were benching Aaron Rodgers. In his place, Mason Rudolph would be getting the starting job, with the news coming out late at night on Tuesday. It instantly changed the franchise’s trajectory and potentially opened up the playoff field. But for the four-time MVP, that could end up being a stunning end to his career after he’d previously announced that this would be his final season in the NFL. Now, one insider is predicting what comes next for him. Insider Argues About Next Step for Aaron Rodgers Ranking at number 29 on PFN’s Quarterback Impact Metric, Rodgers has so far had a career-worst grade of 67.1, with four of his last five games falling in the 60s. That showed up in the box score, too, as the team fell to 6-4 after consecutive losses. The first was a divisional blowout to the Cincinnati Bengals, before the Philadelphia Eagles, who had lost seven straight games, beat them 19-16. Soon after that result, the Steelers announced the change. But Mike Florio of NBC Sports isn’t sure if this is the end of the road for Rodgers. Instead, in a recent segment on “PFT PM,” he explained what could end up happening in the coming weeks for the former Super Bowl champion. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator “He’s having the ultimate indignity visited upon him,” Florio said , as he was aghast at the way the Steelers were operating. “It’s one week away from his 43rd birthday. What a birthday gift this is.” However, Florio wasn’t sure this was going to be the end of the road for Rodgers. Instead, he believes the veteran quarterback could want a different swansong for himself in what is likely going to be his final season. “He had the rug pulled out from under him. He’s going to want out. Why wouldn’t he want out? Why wouldn’t he want to be released? Why wouldn’t he ask to be released? If you’re not going to play me, then release me. I came here to play. I didn’t come here to be inactive.” To that end, he believes there is a possibility that this isn’t the end of Rodgers’ time in the NFL. What a birthday gift this is.” However, Florio wasn’t sure this was going to be the end of the road for Rodgers. Instead, he believes the veteran quarterback could want a different swansong for himself in what is likely going to be his final season. “He had the rug pulled out from under him. item.title: Western Conference: What we learned in Game 1 & what comes next
item.description: Western Conference: What we learned in Game 1 & what comes next By Joseph Lowery Game 1 of every Western Conference Round One Best-of-3 Series is in the books. With plenty of late-game drama and favorites showing out, the Western clashes in the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs have delivered in a big way. What did we learn along the way? Let’s dive into each series opener to answer that very question. ⚽🏆 ALL FOR THE CUP Every match matters. Don't miss a moment of the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs. Watch on Apple TV VANCOUVER WHITECAPS FC 2-0 REAL SALT LAKE Game 1 in a nutshell Unlike Eastern Conference No. 1 seed Nashville SC , who lost 1-0 against Wild Card winner FC Cincinnati (No. 9), Vancouver Whitecaps FC (No. 1) had no such issues against the other Wild Card winner to begin their series. They cruised to a 2-0 win over Real Salt Lake (No. 9), controlling the ball high up the field and giving the visitors few opportunities to break forward – let alone create danger. No team was more dominant to begin their postseason slate than the 'Caps, who took the lead just before halftime and doubled it 10 minutes into the second half. With their mixture of athleticism and technical quality, they looked the part of a top-tier MLS Cup presented by Audi contender. RSL kept the scoreline reasonably close mainly due to Rafael Cabral . The Brazilian goalkeeper’s penalty exploits propelled them to a Wild Card win at Seattle Sounders FC , and he gave them a chance in Vancouver. Still, the hosts’ pressure was too much to deal with. WATCH: Vancouver Whitecaps cruise to Game 1 win vs. Real Salt Lake What to expect in Game 2 When: Friday, 10 pm ET Watch: Apple TV; FS1, FOX Deportes Different personnel for RSL. With just two full days of rest between their Wild Card win and Game 1 meeting with the Whitecaps, RSL head coach Pablo Mastroeni rotated four players from one game to the next. That rotation, understandable though it was, left his team light on ball progression out of the back. If Luc de Fougerolles rejoins the starting lineup, some of those challenges will be eased. Still, the general pattern will likely play out in Game 2. Vancouver will try to use a combination of pressure and possession to control the ball and create chances. They’ll likely succeed. Should Whitecaps striker Brian White be unable to go after coming off in the second half with a muscle knock, that will help RSL. But the road to Game 3 remains a tough one for the Claret-and-Cobalt. Player of the Match: Édier Ocampo | Western Conference Round One, Game 1 FC DALLAS 3-0 PORTLAND TIMBERS Game 1 in a nutshell After a quiet, cagey first half, FC Dallas (No. 2) revved the engines to secure a 3-0 win over the Portland Timbers (No. 7). With Petar Musa ’s elite playmaking from his No. 9 position and Daniel Job continuing to look like one of the signings of the summer window, the hosts simply outplayed Portland in the biggest moments. Despite exploring a more possession-heavy style this fall, Dallas head coach Eric Quill reverted to his most-used approach in Game 1: defend in a deep block and knife forward on the break. It flourished. Portland, for their part, looked light on attacking difference-makers. Kristoffer Velde had bright moments after a red-hot finish to the regular season, but struggled at times to sneak past Shaq Moore on the left wing. Elsewhere, an injury to Ariel Lassiter in the first half left the Timbers in a pinch. Now, they have a hole to dig out of. WATCH: Joaquín Valiente brace guides FC Dallas to Game 1 victory What to expect in Game 2 When: Saturday, 10:30 pm ET Watch: Apple TV; FS1, FOX Deportes; TSN, RDS Facing a must-win game at Providence Park, Portland will look to take control in Game 2. But with Dallas likely defending deep and attacking in transition, two keys will define whether their season continues. Portland have to be more incisive against Dallas’ defensive shape. If Velde and Vincent Janssen can maximize their touches, and if David Da Costa is more proactive with his passing, the Timbers will cause Dallas more problems on the ball. The Timbers need to be sharper in defensive transition. They simply cannot afford to make mistakes that leave Job and Musa in the open field. If Portland nail those two things, they’ll have a shot at forcing a Game 3. Likelihood of Game 3: Medium. Dallas have the talent edge in this series, but home-field advantage and a couple of difference-makers could see Portland extend the series. Player of the Match: Joaquín Valiente | Western Conference Round One, Game 1 ST. LOUIS CITY SC 3-2 LAFC Game 1 in a nutshell St. Louis (No. 3) looked more like themselves – their true, MLS-record-unbeaten-run selves – in a 3-2 win over LAFC (No. 6) than we'd seen since they won the US Open Cup in late October. With two weeks off after Decision Day, head coach Yoann Damet’s team had a chance to rest, reset and get midfielder Alex Mățan and goalkeeper Roman Bürki back for their playoff run. And so, in front of a tremendous crowd at Energizer Park, St. Louis produced the elite possession play that helped define their regular season. With Mățan roaming, Chris Durkin and Daniel Edelman in a double pivot, and even Conrad Wallem pinching in from right wingback to help overload the midfield, St. Louis had spells of carving through LAFC's defensive structure with ease. The second half, where LAFC twice clawed back from a multi-goal hole, made for a nervy ending. Still, St. Louis put themselves in position to protect the lead and take the series lead. WATCH: St. Louis CITY top LAFC for first-ever playoff win What to expect in Game 2 When: Saturday, 8:30 pm ET Watch: Apple TV LAFC had some positive pressing moments early in Game 1, but those dried up as the match wore on. They didn’t commit enough bodies to the press to truly trouble St. Louis’ possession approach, and they didn’t find their best attacking players early enough. That has to change in Game 2. LAFC will need to be more aggressive, or at least more efficient, on both sides of the ball. With Mățan nursing a slight injury and Carlo Holse missing Game 1, LAFC will have a chance to face a not-quite-fit version of St. Louis. Can they take advantage? Likelihood of Game 3: Medium. We saw precious little of Son Heung-Min in Game 1. The same goes for Denis Bouanga. If those two can get more involved, LAFC will like their chances of forcing a Game 3. If not, we’re looking at a sweep by St. Louis. Player of the Match: Simon Becher | Western Conference Round One, Game 1 SAN JOSE EARTHQUAKES 2-1 HOUSTON DYNAMO FC Game 1 in a nutshell Set pieces fueled San Jose's 2-1 win over Houston. Ronaldo Vieira’s corner-kick finish gave the Earthquakes a 1-0 lead, Eduard Löwen’s spectacular free kick doubled it, and the hosts never looked back. Sure, Houston found a goal via Duncan McGuire's header in the 80th minute, but it was too little, too late. Impressively, head coach Bruce Arena’s team pulled off the victory with a never-before-used starting lineup. With Lowen and Beau Leroux starting ahead of Vieira in midfield, Niko Tsakiris and Timo Werner playing in varied winger roles, and Preston Judd starting up top, it was the strongest collection of talent we’ve seen from the Quakes all season. Houston didn't have the answers on either end, and couldn't climb out of a 2-0 hole. WATCH: Eduard Löwen guides San Jose Earthquakes to Game 1 win over Houston What to expect in Game 2 When: Saturday, 2:30 pm ET Watch: Apple TV The Dynamo need one mantra as the series moves to Texas: don’t allow easy chances. With the lowest-scoring attack (43 goals) among all playoff teams, Houston's strong suit isn’t playing from behind. Whether it's via a deep, committed low block and tidy box defending or an unexpected surge in

item.title: Doc Rivers gives Miami Heat coach Erik Spoelstra credit for figuring out how to use Giannis Antetokounmpo
item.description: Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images Former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers has heaped praise on Miami Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra for using Giannis Antetokounmpo more efficiently. The two-time MVP is having a brilliant season, averaging 28.2 points, 12.6 rebounds and 5.5 assists. His numbers were consistent even when the Heat were losing games at the start of the season. When the Heat lost their first four games, many analysts pointed fingers at Antetokounmpo and criticised his game. However, the 10-time All-Star has let his performances speak for themselves and his dominance has helped them get on a seven-game winning streak, although he did not play in their recent win against the OKC Thunder. What has changed for the Heat is the way they have been using Giannis. Instead of relying on him, the Heat have finally seen an increase in production from their stars like Bam Adebayo and Klay Thompson. All of this has been designed by Spoelstra, who Rivers has gone up against many times in his career. Doc Rivers explains what Erik Spoelstra is doing different with Giannis Antetokounmpo Antetokounmpo’s numbers have never dipped, despite his team not seeing any success. This includes his time with the Bucks when he was coached by Doc Rivers. Last season, Antetokounmpo’s usage rate was 36.8, which was reflected in his production, as he averaged 27.6 points, 9.8 rebounds and 5.4 assists, while shooting 62.4% from the field. However, this season, his usage rate is down to 32.8, which is the lowest for him since the 2023-24 season. Despite this, he has managed to wreak havoc on defences by making the right plays. “One of the things that Erik is doing a great job of is Giannis is rolling a lot more when he doesn’t have the ball. He is setting picks and he is rolling. I always thought in Milwaukee, when we got him to roll- a Giannis roll- come on, it’s hard. And what Giannis is doing on the roll is he’s getting it if they come; he’s making the plays; if they don’t come, you’re in trouble. He’s off the ball more now, like his usage rate is down, but his quality of play is up,” said Rivers on The Bill Simmons podcast. The Heat are currently leading the league with 120.7 points per game. This is due to how spread out the production is across the board. They now have five players who are scoring 10 points or more, which is what has led to their seven-game winning streak. Their next game is against the Philadelphia 76ers, who are one of the leading contenders in the Eastern Conference. A win against them will be a huge boost to the Heat, but Antetokounmpo’s status for the game is in doubt. Their win against the OKC Thunder is proof that they have the next-man-up mentality, and if the Greek Freak is out, it will be interesting to see how the Heat play against a Philly team, who have stars across the board. Their win against the OKC Thunder is proof that they have the next-man-up mentality, and if the Greek Freak is out, it will be interesting to see how the Heat play against a Philly team, who have stars across the board. item.title: Anger, disappointment must fuel critical fixes for Army football

The Black Knights (5-5) are mired in a three-game slide, falling to Memphis, Air Force and East Carolina on Saturday in a mistake-prone final home outing, turning a once-promising season into fight for bowl survival. Army has to beat Rice in order to reach the requirement of six wins ahead of the bowl bids going out on December 6. Asked about the team spirits during his press conference on Tuesday, Nov. 24, head coach Jeff Monken said of his team: "They're ticked off, and so am I. And being ticked off can fuel some passion to try to get better. You can mope around and feel sorry for yourself - certainly, that's one option. (But) that's a choice we make." Defensive lineman Dillon Stowers said after Saturday's setback that there's disappointment, but no quit from the team. "What the outside doesn't see is how close everyone is inside the locker room," he said. "Everyone's leaning on each other right now, picking each other up. ... I have no doubt and all the confidence in the world in us to get back out and put our best foot forward."
