Asked about the team spirits during his press conference on Tuesday, Nov. 24, head coach Jeff Monken said of his team: "They're ticked off, and so am I. And being ticked off can fuel some passion to try to get better. You can mope around and feel sorry for yourself - certainly, that's one option. (But) that's a choice we make." Defensive lineman Dillon Stowers said after Saturday's setback that there's disappointment, but no quit from the team. "What the outside doesn't see is how close everyone is inside the locker room," he said. "Everyone's leaning on each other right now, picking each other up. ... I have no doubt and all the confidence in the world in us to get back out and put our best foot forward." Army opened as a 7.5-point favorite, but the spread has dropped to 5.5 in what is anticipated to be another low-scoring contest, the oddsmakers setting 48.5 points as the over/under. Rice (2-9) had lost nine in a row before winning at struggling Temple last Thursday, and Saturday will be the Owls' final game. The last thing Army wants is to ponder a four-game losing streak headed into two weeks of prep for the Navy game, trying to salvage a .500 campaign against a resurgent Midshipmen team, which followed a 2-6 start with wins over Temple and Memphis and is predominant 16.5-point favorite at Charlotte this Saturday. Army football struggles offensively Only weeks earlier, Army's offensive line was judged as one of the top units in the nation as the Black Knights put up major rushing yardage. But injuries sidelined three starters ahead of the East Carolina game and a fourth went down late in the third quarter. The impact resulted in a season-low 180 yards of rushing and total offense of only 264 yards (second worst to the 220 posted a week earlier against Air Force). Senior left guard Kyle Kloska is done for the season, Monken confirmed on Tuesday. Left tackle Henry Appleton was close to being ready for East Carolina, but the coaches decided not to rest him. All-American center candidate Brady Small was injured against Air Force and watched from the sidelines on Saturday, wearing a protective boot and using a coaster to support his leg. Right guard Paolo Gennarelli got hurt against the Pirates, visited the medical tent and was spotted afterward trying to test his mobility but did not return. That left right tackle Teddy Williams as the lone healthy starter. In place of the injured linemen were Xavier Archawski, Ben Britton, Chuck Johnson and Jonah Zimmerman. Monken said Tuesday he was hopeful for the return of Appleton, Small and Gennarelli, but mid-week statements and posted depth charts have not always lined up with starts. Monken went into a long explanation about the resulting problems, essentially saying some gaps for running backs are not being pried open wide enough at times, or gaps aren't being closed for attacking linebackers and blitzing safeties. "We just didn't do it well enough, consistently enough," he noted. He also mentioned some outside runs were clipped short on heel tackles, and some option reads were probably mistaken. "There's things like that, throughout the course of the game that we've got to improve, get better at and execute more effectively," he said. As for the continuity between the existing backs and basically a new cast of linemen, he said no matter who's playing, there's got to be a trust factor that the calls are being executed properly. "There's a lot of things that can take a play the wrong direction," Monken said. item.title: Victor Wembanyama faces untimely injury concern before showdown with Luka Doncic
item.description: Victor Wembanyama faces untimely injury concern before showdown with Luka Doncic originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Victor Wembanyama has spent the opening weeks of the NBA season making a compelling case to win his first MVP award. The San Antonio Spurs superstar has delivered some enormous individual performances while helping his team emerge as one of the league's most dangerous contenders. However, an untimely injury concern has introduced some uncertainty entering Thanksgiving weekend. Wembanyama missed Monday's 123-107 victory over the Sacramento Kings because of back tightness and is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Portland Trail Blazers , according to Reuters. While the Spurs demonstrated their impressive depth against Sacramento, basketball fans have another reason to closely monitor Wembanyama's availability. A highly anticipated meeting with Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers awaits Friday. Two superstars are separating themselves The NBA's latest official MVP Ladder, published last week, placed Doncic first and Wembanyama second. Miami Heat superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo occupied the third spot, but Friday's game could provide an early opportunity for the two leading candidates to make statements against each other. Victor Wembanyama (back) listed questionable for Wednesday. — Underdog NBA (@UnderdogNBA) November 25, 2026 Wembanyama is averaging 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds and 3.9 blocks this season. He recently produced separate performances of 50 and 52 points, illustrating just how dramatically his offensive capabilities have developed. His ability to influence games defensively while delivering enormous scoring totals makes his emergence particularly remarkable. Perhaps equally impressive is San Antonio's 15-3 record. Wembanyama's individual production is translating into victories, an important consideration when evaluating legitimate MVP candidates rather than simply identifying the league's most productive players. The Spurs have little reason to take unnecessary risks with their franchise centerpiece, particularly this early in a promising season. item.title: Imesha Dulani, Sathya Sandeepani star as Sri Lanka beat Ireland to win Women's Emerging Nations Trophy
item.description: Sri Lanka produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat Ireland by six wickets and clinch the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy 2026 on Wednesday. Imesha Dulani starred with an unbeaten 44 as Sri Lanka comfortably chased down the 97-run target in just 12.4 overs in the final at the Karwan Sports Club. The victory marked Sri Lanka's first title in the tournament's history, succeeding Thailand, who won the inaugural edition in 2025. Sri Lanka's bowlers bundle out Ireland for 96 After opting to bat first, Ireland endured a disastrous start, losing captain Gaby Lewis in the opening over at 5/1. The early setback soon turned into a collapse as they slipped to 10/2 before struggling to recover. Sri Lanka's disciplined bowling attack kept the pressure firmly on Ireland, reducing them to 54/6 inside 12 overs. Alana Dalzell emerged as Ireland's top scorer with 24 off 25 deliveries, while Louise Little contributed 15 off 17 balls. Georgina Dempsey also chipped in with 13, but Ireland failed to build meaningful partnerships and were eventually bowled out for 96 in 19.3 overs. Sathya Sandeepani was the standout performer with the ball, claiming four wickets for just 13 runs in her four overs. Kavisha Dilhari, Sugandika Kumari, Nimasha Meepage and Chethana Vimukthi picked up a wicket apiece, while two run-outs further dented Ireland's innings. Imesha Dulani guides Sri Lanka to title Chasing 97, Sri Lanka made an aggressive start but suffered a brief setback after Sanjana Kavindi departed for 25 off 22 balls. Captain Harshitha Samarawickrama was dismissed for a golden duck on the following delivery, leaving Sri Lanka at 35/2. Ireland attempted to stage a comeback through Kia McCartney and Cara Murray, who picked up two wickets each to reduce Sri Lanka to 69/4 in the ninth over. However, Dulani held her nerve and ensured there were no further hiccups. She remained unbeaten on 44, while Dilhari provided valuable support with an unbeaten 16 off just 10 deliveries. The pair stitched together an unbroken 30-run partnership to take Sri Lanka to 99/4 in 12.4 overs, sealing a convincing six-wicket victory and the championship trophy. Brief Scores Ireland Women: 96 all out in 19.3 overs (Alana Dalzell 24, Louise Little 15; Sathya Sandeepani 4/13) lost to Sri Lanka Women: 99/4 in 12.4 overs (Imesha Dulani 44*, Sanjana Kavindi 25; Kia McCartney 2/16, Cara Murray 2/38) by six wickets.

item.title: Browns’ home-field advantage could be on display on Sunday Night Football vs. the Raiders
item.description: The dedication of the Cleveland Browns fan base has been a huge advantage for the players on the field throughout the team’s history. The fans do a great job of cheering the team on while also making it a challenging environment for opposing teams. The Browns are 4-0 at home so far this season, and the team had a game-winning fourth-quarter drive in each of those victories. While on-field performance is certainly the main factor in these wins, it cannot be overlooked that the atmosphere at Huntington Bank Field played a role in the team’s ability to finish these games strong. Consistency at home can build confidence too and help to establish a winning culture. When fans recognize that the atmosphere makes a difference and players are confident that it gives them an extra edge, it can have a positive impact on the team’s performance on the field. With four home games left against the Las Vegas Raiders, Cincinnati Bengals, Atlanta Falcons, and Indianapolis Colts, Cleveland hopes to finish out the season 8-0 in front of the home crowd. Let me know what you think in the comments – Is Cleveland’s home field advantage a real factor? Join the conversation! item.title: Exeter defender Harper 'honoured' by Kenya cap
item.description: Vincent Harper is on a season-long loan at Exeter City from Walsall [Shutterstock] Vincent Harper says he relished the chance to play for Kenya during the international break. The Exeter City wing-back, on loan from League Two rivals Walsall, came on in his country's 2-1 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier loss to South Africa in Nairobi last week. It was his second cap this season, having played 90 minutes against Rwanda in a friendly last month. "It's a massive honour," Harper told BBC Radio Devon. "My parents were both born there, it just feels almost like you're repaying back, not to them but also to the whole country. "It's a lot of pressure at the same time, but overall it's just a big honour." Harper has played 13 times since returning to Exeter this season - he had a two-year spell at St James Park before he joined Walsall in the summer of 2025. The former Bristol City youth player made his English Football League debut when he moved to Exeter from Eastleigh in 2023 and went on to play 65 times in all competitions before moving to the Midlands. "I think it just shows you the next level or the level you need to be at to play consistently at an international level," he added. "It's very intense and very quick and you're playing with the best of the best of the country so you've got to definitely be at your 'A' game. "If you make one mistake then you'll definitely be punished." Exeter City bring in Harper and Samuel on loan Harper started all seven of Exeter's games after arriving back at the club. But while he was away on international duty in October, Exeter hit a rich vein of form and he has not been able to get back into the starting line-up. He is hopeful he can force his way back into a side that has been one of League Two's in-form teams over the past two months - Exeter have risen from close to the relegation zone to the brink of the play-off places after just one loss in their past 10 games in all competitions. "It's a bit of a frustrating one," he admitted. "Before the first internationals I was heavily involved and then the boys started doing well while I was away. "It's nice to see the boys doing well, but I want to be more part of it and spend more time on the pitch and show them what I can do. "But overall it's good to see the team winning and although I might not get as many minutes as I want, it's nice to come on here and there and play my part as well." item.title: Pep Guardiola confirms he will coach a national team next as USMNT fans hope for return to management in USA
item.description: Pep Guardiola confirms he will coach a national team next as USMNT fans hope for return to management in USA originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The greatest manager of this generation has already been mulling the avenue for his return. Pep Guardiola has been out of a job since departing Manchester City in the summer, and while it seems he's enjoying his time off, he has clearly been thinking about where he wants to end up next. It would be a first for Guardiola, who has never managed internationally before, but he has many national federations on high alert. Most notably, the U.S. national team has reportedly made Guardiola its top choice, and will likely spend the remainder of 2026 hoping to either convince him to take the job immediately, or develop a pathway for him to take it when he's ready. If Guardiola is going to take over the USMNT, this was a promising first step towards that eventuality, even if a small one. MORE: All the latest USMNT news | Was Pochettino a success with the USMNT? Pep Guardiola says his next job will be with a national team Speaking with his former Barcelona teammate Romario on his YouTube channel RomarioTV , Pep Guardiola confirmed that his next role will be in international football. When asked if there was a club he would like to coach that he hasn't, Guardiola interjected. "A national team, which is my next step," he said. The 55-year-old has never coached internationally before. He confirmed during the interview that he was approached by the Italian federation (FIGC) over the summer, but turned down the opportunity because he wanted to take time off and had only just departed Man City. "I spoke with them," Guardiola said of the FIGC. “It was an honor. I even feel bad or ashamed to say no to a country like Italy. It is one of the biggest honors I’ve had that they thought of me as the right man to manage Italy. But they found me in a moment when I needed to stop. "If they had come in one or two years time, probably I would have taken it." MORE: USMNT 2027 schedule, fixtures, dates, competitions, and more Could Pep Guardiola coach the USMNT? There is a real pathway for Pep Guardiola to coach the United States men's national team, if he wants it. Mauricio Pochettino, who departed last week to take over at Manchester United , has laid the groundwork for another top manager like Guardiola to take over in his wake. The manner of Pochettino's departure will surely put other top managers on high alert. The Argentine was highly emotional at his exit press conference, saying that the choice to leave was "the most difficult decision of my career" and speaking extremely well of the federation and staff he worked alongside. Speaking through tears, Pochettino said that the federation "made me feel really happy doing my job, sharing an amazing project, being part of this family." If Guardiola is going to take over the USMNT, this was a promising first step towards that eventuality, even if a small one. MORE: All the latest USMNT news | Was Pochettino a success with the USMNT? Pep Guardiola says his next job will be with a national team Speaking with his former Barcelona teammate Romario on his YouTube channel RomarioTV , Pep Guardiola confirmed that his next role will be in international football. When asked if there was a club he would like to coach that he hasn't, Guardiola interjected. "A national team, which is my next step," he said. The 55-year-old has never coached internationally before. He confirmed during the interview that he was approached by the Italian federation (FIGC) over the summer, but turned down the opportunity because he wanted to take time off and had only just departed Man City. "I spoke with them," Guardiola said of the FIGC. “It was an honor. I even feel bad or ashamed to say no to a country like Italy. It is one of the biggest honors I’ve had that they thought of me as the right man to manage Italy. But they found me in a moment when I needed to stop. "If they had come in one or two years time, probably I would have taken it." MORE: USMNT 2027 schedule, fixtures, dates, competitions, and more Could Pep Guardiola coach the USMNT? There is a real pathway for Pep Guardiola to coach the United States men's national team, if he wants it. Mauricio Pochettino, who departed last week to take over at Manchester United , has laid the groundwork for another top manager like Guardiola to take over in his wake. The manner of Pochettino's departure will surely put other top managers on high alert. The Argentine was highly emotional at his exit press conference, saying that the choice to leave was "the most difficult decision of my career" and speaking extremely well of the federation and staff he worked alongside. Speaking through tears, Pochettino said that the federation "made me feel really happy doing my job, sharing an amazing project, being part of this family." Pochettino's efforts in the United States may not have brought tangible growth on the pitch in terms of results, but he elevated the program's culture and built a much larger player pool from which to choose possible starters. Additionally, there is time to work out something with Guardiola. The Spaniard has said multiple times he wishes to take a full year off from management. To that end, there is just one singular international break between Pochettino's departure at the end of the November window and the start of the CONCACAF Gold Cup in the summer — an interim boss could be named to handle the CONCACAF Nations League finals in the March window before Guardiola takes over in June. This would give Pep time to enjoy the remainder of his hiatus, while also having the certainty of knowing what his next job will be, allowing both him and the federation to prepare for his eventual start date. Guardiola also has an affinity for the United States. As Sporting News reporter Dom Farrell put it , "Guardiola lived in New York during his 2012/13 sabbatical and is enamoured with U.S. sporting culture, especially basketball. He became good friends with Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla during his time at City." There is still a very long way to go in this regard, and Guardiola's level of interest in the role is still unknown. But the fact he has not publicly turned it down yet indicates he probably thinks there is at least some level of realistic future between the two.

item.title: How the Miami Heat saved the season after a terrible start
item.description: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Heat ended last season in an awkward spot. For the fourth straight year, they found themselves in the NBA Play-In Tournament. Unfortunately, this was the first time they couldn’t make it out. They have a S-Tier leading man calling the shots, a battle-tested defensive anchor , and a culture of winning in the ugliest ways possible. Their roster, while nothing special, was far from the dregs of the association. It contained a good blend of young bucks and proven veterans. If the injury gods smiled in their favor and a couple of prospects took meaningful steps forward, the Heat could have run it back and flirted with 50 wins. And with their knack for upsets, maybe a postseason series victory would have followed. However, the Heat, like the Minnesota Timberwolves , remembered that they didn’t come to the table to nickel and dime their way through the nights. In Miami, they play for keeps. Win big, or go bankrupt trying. So, when Giannis Antetokounmpo finally became available, the Heat swung for the fences – trading the farm in the hopes that the singular excellence of the former two-time MVP , coupled with Bam Adebayo and the scrapes that remained would be enough to vault the team into true contention. Through nine games, it looked like they would be filing for Chapter 7. The Heat were 3-6 and floundering, while their contemporaries (the Detroit Pistons, Boston Celtics, and Philadelphia 76ers) were thriving out the gate. But fast forward to today, and it looks like the big bet they placed may have been the right call. What Changed For The Miami Heat? After their 10-point win over the depleted Oklahoma City Thunder, the Heat are winners of their last seven games and now sit at No. 6 in the Eastern Conference – fully within striking distance of the conference’s upper echelon. In a team sport like basketball, it’s foolish to point to one variable as the reason for positive change, as so many factors contribute to success, but it is hard not to watch this team and look at the ring leader as the catalyst: Erik Spoelstra. item.content:encoded: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Heat ended last season in an awkward spot. For the fourth straight year, they found themselves in the NBA Play-In Tournament. Unfortunately, this was the first time they couldn’t make it out. They have a S-Tier leading man calling the shots, a battle-tested defensive anchor , and a culture of winning in the ugliest ways possible. Their roster, while nothing special, was far from the dregs of the association. It contained a good blend of young bucks and proven veterans. If the injury gods smiled in their favor and a couple of prospects took meaningful steps forward, the Heat could have run it back and flirted with 50 wins. And with their knack for upsets, maybe a postseason series victory would have followed. However, the Heat, like the Minnesota Timberwolves , remembered that they didn’t come to the table to nickel and dime their way through the nights. In Miami, they play for keeps. Win big, or go bankrupt trying. So, when Giannis Antetokounmpo finally became available, the Heat swung for the fences – trading the farm in the hopes that the singular excellence of the former two-time MVP , coupled with Bam Adebayo and the scrapes that remained would be enough to vault the team into true contention. Through nine games, it looked like they would be filing for Chapter 7. The Heat were 3-6 and floundering, while their contemporaries (the Detroit Pistons, Boston Celtics, and Philadelphia 76ers) were thriving out the gate. But fast forward to today, and it looks like the big bet they placed may have been the right call. What Changed For The Miami Heat? After their 10-point win over the depleted Oklahoma City Thunder, the Heat are winners of their last seven games and now sit at No. 6 in the Eastern Conference – fully within striking distance of the conference’s upper echelon. In a team sport like basketball, it’s foolish to point to one variable as the reason for positive change, as so many factors contribute to success, but it is hard not to watch this team and look at the ring leader as the catalyst: Erik Spoelstra. Spoelstra may be the best coach in basketball. Heck, he may be one of the five best coaches that ever lived (we know he’s at least one of the top 15 ). Spoelstra is innovative enough to turn oranges into lemonade. No, that’s not a typo that was missed by my editor. The creative lens Spoelstra is able to analyze the game through literally defies everything we know about the human experience. With an average age of 28.8 years old , the Heat have the second-oldest team in the NBA (behind only the Golden State Warriors). That is bad news bears in today’s game – one that rewards athleticism, pace, and physicality. Spoelstra realized it was time to demote the veterans that most coaches would remain beholden too. His biggest change was taking Andrew Wiggins (31 years old), and putting Pelle Larsson in his place (25). And when he’s been hurt, instead of reverting back to Wiggins, Spoelstra simply plugs in Myron Gardner (25) in his place. A former second rounder and undrafted player in the place of a former first overall pick, NBA champion, and the third-highest paid player on the team’s payroll. Wiggins wasn’t the only casualty. Bobby Portis’ minutes are down, and Tim Hardaway Jr. is basically out of the rotation entirely. Along with Larsson and Gardner, those minutes are being eaten up by the youthful vigor of second round rookie Ryan Conwell (22). Despite hearing 36 names called before his on draft night, Conwell is seventh among rookies in minutes per game (26.2) in their last seven games. Delegating hustle duties to fresher legs lessens the burdens on Antetokounmpo, Adebayo, Klay Thompson, and Davion Mitchell’s shoulders, and enables them to focus more energy on scoring the ball. The Heat’s effective field goal percentage is up 4.8% over the last seven games. Spoelstra has also made a key strategic shift. To start the season, the Heat were doing a lot of hard hedging with ball screens involving their bigs. The idea is that since they start two center-sized players, they could afford for one of them to play these actions more aggressively, since the other one would be there to clean it up. The idea wasn’t a bad one, in theory, but playing this way asks the three guys not involved in the action to do a lot of flying around to cover up the gaps. Antetokounmpo, now in Year 14, has a lot of tread on his tires, and scrambling around possession after possession isn’t necessarily high on his list of priorities. So, instead of trying to fit a square peg into a round hole, Spoelstra scrapped the idea and started switching everything (except actions involving Portis, which the Heat continue to hedge). This asks Antetokounmpo and company to do a lot less rotating around, and it still lets the Heat benefit from their twin tower configuration (when one of them is switched onto the perimeter, the other can still lurk around the painted area). As a result, the Heat are forcing fewer turnovers (the tradeoff of playing a less aggressive style). However, by switching everything, it is easier for them to keep the ball in front of them, and so the Heat’s opponents are shooting far worse from the floor than they were before. And again, it conserves more energy, so the Heat have their legs under them on their own shots. Due to the constraints of the written medium, we can’t dissect ALL of Spoelstra’s game-changing tweaks, but here are a couple of other developments you can see his fingerprint on: convincing Antetokounmpo into operating more off-the-ball, squeezing the last ounce of magic out of Thompson, and gradually helping mold Mitchell from bust to baller. How Good Are The Heat Actually? The good news for the Heat is that there are some aspects that will improve with time. Despite rostering Antetokounmpo and Adebayo – who have 11 All-Defensive Teams between the two of them – Miami is currently 24th in defensive rating. The adjustments the Heat have made with minute allocation and scheme have helped bump them from 26th in this category in their first nine games to 17th in the last seven, but they are still being hurt by some bad luck. This season, the Heat are surrendering a whopping 45.6% on wide open threes (per NBA.com). That is 2.7% than the next highest team, and 6.1% higher than the league average. The Heat under Spoelstra tend to give up more threes in order to prioritize protecting the rim, but defense has nothing to do with how well opponents shoot on open looks. That’s just luck. If/when that number regresses to the mean (no team has allowed higher than 43% on these shots for an entire season), Miami’s defensive rating will automatically improve. Unfortunately, the Heat have also been the beneficiary of some good luck. According to Estimated Plus-Minus, they have had the third-easiest strength of schedule. They have also lost the fourth-fewest dollars to player injuries (per Spotrac). Antetokounmpo and Thompson have only missed one game each. Mitchell and Adebayo have been available for every game. What happens if one or two of those guys is out for an extended stretch? This isn’t a super deep team. More than likely, the conflicting noise between their negative shooting luck and positive schedule/injury history thus far is a wash. To me, the pace this Heat are currently on (51 wins) seems about right. They are a good team that, even with Spoelstra’s magic touch, still has some glaring flaws (on-ball creation, offensive variety, depth) in a conference filled with them. If they draw the first round opponent or injuries cause them to fall into the play-in tournament for the fifth straight year, another early exit could be in their future. But if Spoelstra keeps putting on a coaching clinic in the best league on the planet and Antetokounmpo can stay healthy enough to match him for a whole postseason, maybe, just maybe, the Heat can return to the NBA Finals for the first time

item.title: Jack Harvey named Special Advisor at Dreyer & Reinbold, will sit out 2027 Indy 500
item.description: Motorsport photo IndyCar driver and FOX Sports reporter Jack Harvey has announced that he will step aside from competing in the 2027 Indianapolis 500, shifting his focus toward a return to the cockpit in 2028. The update comes roughly six weeks after the 33-year-old Briton first revealed in mid-October that he had been diagnosed with cancer , a point at which he still hoped to be on the grid in St. Petersburg and race in May. While stepping back from driving duties next year, Harvey will remain closely tied to Dreyer & Reinbold Racing as a Special Advisor while continuing his broadcast work alongside his colleagues at FOX. In a statement shared on social media, Harvey explained the reasoning behind his decision: “Preparing for the Indianapolis 500 requires daily dedication, consistency, and an unwavering commitment. It is a responsibility I have never taken lightly, and I have the utmost respect for the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, the race itself, DRR and my fellow competitors. “As I look to 2027, I recognize I won’t be able to dedicate myself to preparing for the 111th Indianapolis 500 at the level I expect and that this incredible event demands. With that in mind, I’ve made the decision to step aside from competing in 2027 and will focus on preparing for the 2028 event. “While I won’t be behind the wheel, I’m excited to continue my relationship with Dreyer & Reinbold Racing in a new role as Special Advisor. This team has shown me tremendous support and has worked tirelessly both on and off the track. I look forward to returning that same commitment as they make their return to full-time IndyCar competition. “2027 is shaping up to be an incredible year for our sport. The momentum is real, and I can’t wait to reunite with my colleagues at FOX and get back to work.” Dreyer & Reinbold Racing also issued a statement supporting Harvey’s recovery and welcoming him into his new role with the organization: “Jack has been an incredible part of our team and family. His health and well being will always come first. We look forward to supporting Jack’s continued recovery and look forward to seeing him back behind the wheel. In the meantime, we’re excited to welcome Jack into his new role as Special Advisor, where his experience, perspective and passion for the sport will be invaluable as we continue to build toward the future.” Read Also: IndyCar adds Kansas Speedway to 2027 schedule in joint NASCAR weekend IndyCar driver and Fox Sports reporter Jack Harvey announces cancer diagnosis To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Travis and Jason Kelce say there’s an ‘insane’ rule in the NFL they now want changing
item.description: Photo by David Calvert/Getty Images for American Century Investments Roger Goodell has a good relationship with Travis and Jason Kelce, having already featured on one of their podcasts in the past. This could provide them with the ideal gateway to vent their frustrations with the NFL over the crackback block ruling. There are aspects of a crackback block that are legal, but players can also be penalised for it if not performed to the league’s guidelines. Travis Kelce is a player who will have the crackback block in his arsenal of plays on the field. The tight end has, however, hit out at the NFL for overprotecting players who do not have possession of the football during a game. Travis and Jason Kelce call for NFL to make the crackback block fully legal The crackback block can be a huge advantage to an offense if pulled off correctly, but players are risking a penalty against their team. This is something that the Kelce brothers feel needs looking into by those in charge of the NFL. “You’re running scot-free on the kickoff. You’ve got to have your antennas up. This is why crackbacks should be legal, because guys just have to be on your P’s and Q’s. Keep your head on a swivel, man. You’re on the field,” said Travis on the New Heights podcast. https://open.spotify.com/embed?uri=spotify%3Aepisode%3A1fdxz4celqmI6CnK4BjWfT Jason: “The idea that you’re defenceless when you’re running on the field is insane to me, the ball carrier isn’t right there. You’re not extending for a catch, you’re not throwing a ball, you’re just running, why is there not an onus on defending yourself?” “It’s the dumbest rule change of all time, I hate it.” Travis Kelce has already questioned the NFL’s Hawk-Eye system , with the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end not pleased with the new technology being introduced into the game. The crackback block is certainly not something new, but the brothers are both keen for a change to the rule. The pair clearly enjoy the physical side of the game, but the NFL are keen to provide as much protection to its players in this day and age due to the new studies showing the impact the game has had on the brains of former players. item.title: Geno Auriemma’s UConn matches unfortunate program record seen only once this century
item.description: Geno Auriemma’s UConn matches unfortunate program record seen only once this century originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Geno Auriemma has sounded the alarms with his UConn team -- and the Huskies' season is only seven games old. With Thanksgiving looming, maybe Auriemma and the Huskies will be happy not to see one another for a few days. The holiday will come after Tuesday night's 65-56 defeat to the top-ranked South Carolina Gamecocks at Mohegan Sun Arena, in which the Huskies missed 14 of 20 layups and allowed an uncharacteristic 16-0 Gamecocks run at the end of the second quarter that ultimately decided the game. "I've never had a team at the University of Connecticut that misses this many layups or has (as) many stupid fouls as this team," Auriemma said after Tuesday's loss. "So all you're doing is hurting yourself." UConn off to its joint-worst start this century The Huskies fell to 4-3 with Tuesday night's defeat in Uncasville. That matches the worst start for Auriemma's storied program since the 2023-24 season. Before that, the Huskies had not started a season this slowly since 1986, when Auriemma was beginning his second season at the school. UConn went on to miss the tournament that season and the one after before kickstarting its prolonged run of dominance in the sport. "It's just a very, very, very immature team, basketball-wise," Auriemma said. "And maybe in general, I don't know." “Maybe it's just too much for them. … Maybe I overstated what kind of team we had mentally.” Geno Auriemma did not hold back on the state of UConn basketball Tuesday night. The Huskies are off to their worst start in 40 years. https://t.co/1232ggX82b — Meghan L. Hall (@ItsMeghanLHall) November 25, 2026 It's true that this is a young UConn team. Last year's Huskies relied on the sharpshooting and veteran leadership of eventual No. 1 draft pick Azzi Fudd; the year before, Paige Bueckers was in her last year of NCAA eligibility and signed off with a championship. This UConn team has only two seniors -- and one, KK Arnold, did not play Tuesday. The Huskies' unquestioned best player is a junior. But after that, UConn's second-best player thus far is freshman guard Jovana Popovic. Maybe Auriemma has a point -- this Huskies team needs time to gel and mature. They have a few months to do so before the NCAA Tournament, and the legendary head coach's "tough love" approach has paid dividends before. But as it stands, UConn will require a significant turnaround to reach the heights that Auriemma has long expected of his program. item.title: Could Aaron Rodgers demand his release? 1 team should be all-in on him
item.description: Aaron Rodgers’ future with the Pittsburgh Steelers suddenly looks uncertain after the veteran quarterback was informed that he would be benched for NFL Week 12. Stunner: The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday’s game against the Broncos. Sources say this was a coach’s decision. But Rodgers has struggled and now Mike McCarthy is making a change. https://t.co/wPSeMX3lmq — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 25, 2026 The decision to turn to Mason Rudolph for the Black Friday matchup against the Denver Broncos raises questions about how Rodgers will respond and whether he wants to remain in Pittsburgh. If the situation leads to a release, there is one AFC team that should seriously consider pursuing him: the New England Patriots. MORE: Bold predictions for Week 12 of 2026 NFL season Rodgers’ benching could lead to questions about his future in Pittsburgh Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) leaves the field after the game at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Late Tuesday night, Rodgers was informed that he would be replaced by Rudolph for the Steelers’ Week 12 matchup against Denver. The situation took another interesting turn Wednesday morning when Rodgers did not show up at the Pittsburgh facility . That naturally raises questions about whether Rodgers intends to stick around after losing his starting job. At this stage of his career, being moved to the bench could change how he views his future with the organization, especially with the season entering a critical stretch. Rodgers has performed better than expected this season, putting up respectable numbers despite having limited offensive talent around him. While Pittsburgh has decided to make a change at quarterback, there is still a case to be made that Rodgers could help another team looking for an upgrade at the position. If Rodgers decides he no longer wants to remain in Pittsburgh, requesting his release could become a possibility. Whether the Steelers would grant that request is another question, but a potential separation would immediately create interest around the veteran quarterback. Patriots should pursue Rodgers if he becomes available Nov 1, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) throws a pass during the fourth quarter of an NFL game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium. item.content:encoded: Aaron Rodgers’ future with the Pittsburgh Steelers suddenly looks uncertain after the veteran quarterback was informed that he would be benched for NFL Week 12. Stunner: The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday’s game against the Broncos. Sources say this was a coach’s decision. But Rodgers has struggled and now Mike McCarthy is making a change. https://t.co/wPSeMX3lmq — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 25, 2026 The decision to turn to Mason Rudolph for the Black Friday matchup against the Denver Broncos raises questions about how Rodgers will respond and whether he wants to remain in Pittsburgh. If the situation leads to a release, there is one AFC team that should seriously consider pursuing him: the New England Patriots. MORE: Bold predictions for Week 12 of 2026 NFL season Rodgers’ benching could lead to questions about his future in Pittsburgh Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) leaves the field after the game at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Late Tuesday night, Rodgers was informed that he would be replaced by Rudolph for the Steelers’ Week 12 matchup against Denver. The situation took another interesting turn Wednesday morning when Rodgers did not show up at the Pittsburgh facility . That naturally raises questions about whether Rodgers intends to stick around after losing his starting job. At this stage of his career, being moved to the bench could change how he views his future with the organization, especially with the season entering a critical stretch. Rodgers has performed better than expected this season, putting up respectable numbers despite having limited offensive talent around him. While Pittsburgh has decided to make a change at quarterback, there is still a case to be made that Rodgers could help another team looking for an upgrade at the position. If Rodgers decides he no longer wants to remain in Pittsburgh, requesting his release could become a possibility. Whether the Steelers would grant that request is another question, but a potential separation would immediately create interest around the veteran quarterback. Patriots should pursue Rodgers if he becomes available Nov 1, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) throws a pass during the fourth quarter of an NFL game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The New England Patriots are an intriguing potential landing spot if Rodgers becomes available. Their chances of winning the AFC East may be gone, but they remain in the hunt for an AFC Wild Card spot. The biggest problem is the quarterback position. Drake Maye is expected to be unavailable for the foreseeable future, leaving New England in a difficult position as it tries to remain competitive. Without Maye or a significant upgrade at quarterback, the Patriots could have a difficult time keeping their postseason hopes alive. Rodgers would give New England an experienced option capable of providing stability at quarterback. Considering how he has performed this season despite the limitations around him in Pittsburgh, the Patriots could view him as an opportunity to improve their chances of staying in the playoff race. Of course, a potential move would depend on Rodgers becoming available and the Patriots showing interest. But if he does demand his release and the Steelers grant it, there should be a conversation between Rodgers and New England. The Patriots have a reason to explore the possibility, and Rodgers could have an opportunity to join a team still fighting for a postseason spot. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Do the Royals need more starting pitching depth?
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 25: Bryce Miller #50 of the Seattle Mariners pitches during the second inning against the Los Angeles Angels at T-Mobile Park on September 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Royals made it clear that adding starting pitching was a priority this offseason. After finishing second in baseball with a 3.55 ERA for their starting pitchers in 2024, the Royals fell to sixth-worst in the league at 4.58 this year. Thirteen different pitchers made a start, as the Royals were plagued with injuries. J.J. Picollo told reporters he planned to be aggressive in acquisitions after a disappointing 2026 campaign. He followed up by trading All-Star third baseman Maikel Garcia to Seattle in a six-player trade for starting pitchers Bryce Miller and Logan Evans, and reliever Jose Ferrer. The additions of Miller and Evans give the Royals more options in the rotation, but how much have they really improved their depth? The Royals have several pitchers who could factor into the starting rotation in 2027, but there are questions about the health, durability, and track records of many of them. Let’s take a look at the candidates and where they fit. The locks Michael Wacha was the team’s most dependable starter in 2026, an All-Star and a workhorse who led the American League with 200.2 innings. The 35-year-old has been a remarkably consistent presence in the rotation since joining Kansas City, arguably one of their best free agent signings ever. He finished last season strong with a 2.66 ERA in 13 starts after the All-Star break, and the Royals are hoping he can continue that performance into the last year of his contract. Bryce Miller was really terrific in 2024, but has a 4.82 ERA in 209 innings in the two seasons combined since then. He battled elbow issues in 2025, then missed the first six weeks of this season with an oblique injury. The Royals are banking on him being healthy and returning to the form he showed in 2024 when he posted the eighth-lowest ERA in baseball . He has the potential to miss bats – his 24.3 percent strikeout rate that year would have ranked third-best in Royals history, behind only Cole Ragans in 2024 and Zack Greinke in 2009. He began throwing his cutter more, improving the success of all his pitches. item.content:encoded: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 25: Bryce Miller #50 of the Seattle Mariners pitches during the second inning against the Los Angeles Angels at T-Mobile Park on September 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Royals made it clear that adding starting pitching was a priority this offseason. After finishing second in baseball with a 3.55 ERA for their starting pitchers in 2024, the Royals fell to sixth-worst in the league at 4.58 this year. Thirteen different pitchers made a start, as the Royals were plagued with injuries. J.J. Picollo told reporters he planned to be aggressive in acquisitions after a disappointing 2026 campaign. He followed up by trading All-Star third baseman Maikel Garcia to Seattle in a six-player trade for starting pitchers Bryce Miller and Logan Evans, and reliever Jose Ferrer. The additions of Miller and Evans give the Royals more options in the rotation, but how much have they really improved their depth? The Royals have several pitchers who could factor into the starting rotation in 2027, but there are questions about the health, durability, and track records of many of them. Let’s take a look at the candidates and where they fit. The locks Michael Wacha was the team’s most dependable starter in 2026, an All-Star and a workhorse who led the American League with 200.2 innings. The 35-year-old has been a remarkably consistent presence in the rotation since joining Kansas City, arguably one of their best free agent signings ever. He finished last season strong with a 2.66 ERA in 13 starts after the All-Star break, and the Royals are hoping he can continue that performance into the last year of his contract. Bryce Miller was really terrific in 2024, but has a 4.82 ERA in 209 innings in the two seasons combined since then. He battled elbow issues in 2025, then missed the first six weeks of this season with an oblique injury. The Royals are banking on him being healthy and returning to the form he showed in 2024 when he posted the eighth-lowest ERA in baseball . He has the potential to miss bats – his 24.3 percent strikeout rate that year would have ranked third-best in Royals history, behind only Cole Ragans in 2024 and Zack Greinke in 2009. Noah Cameron figured something out after he began calling his own pitches in July. From July 24 on, he had a 2.58 ERA in 12 games, the 11th-lowest in baseball over that time. He began throwing his cutter more, improving the success of all his pitches. He is the definition of a ‘crafty lefty,’ and while he may not have overpowering stuff, his ability to mix pitches and keep hitters guessing makes him a valuable part of the rotation. Seth Lugo raised alarm bells with a 6.62 ERA over his last 17 starts, the second consecutive year his numbers have gone off the rails in the second half of the season. He had the seventh-lowest strikeout rate among qualified starters, and while he has never been one to miss bats, it leaves him little room for error. The 37-year-old is entering the last year of his contract (assuming the Royals decline his $17 million option for 2028), and the question is how much he has left in the tank. Rotation candidates Randy Dobnak resurrected his career with the Royals this year after pitching in just six MLB games over the previous three seasons combined. In his first 10 games he posted a 1.92 ERA, only faltering at the end to finish at 3.51. It was the second-best ERA by any Royals starter, but there are questions about how sustainable his performance was. After he joined the rotation on July 2, he had the fifth-lowest strikeout rate in baseball. Tony Gonsolin was signed late in the year and pitched in just one game, but the Royals picked up his $2.5 million option for next year to get a look at what he can do. The 32-year-old right-hander was an All-Star with the Dodgers in 2022, but injuries have derailed his career since then. He missed all of 2024 following Tommy John surgery, then made just seven starts in 2025 before undergoing another elbow procedure involving an internal brace. He’s a decent reclamation project, but the Royals shouldn’t be counting on him at this point considering his injury past. Daniel Lynch IV will get a look as a starter after excelling in the bullpen the last two seasons. Lynch made ten starts late in the year with an unimpressive 6.53 ERA and a very low strikeout rate of 12 percent. He was also a starter from 2021-22, and posted a 5.32 ERA in 42 starts over that time. J.J. Picollo said the Royals recognize the difficulty of transitioning back to a starting role late in the season after having success in the bullpen, but that “he does believe he can start, and we think he did enough over the last two months to compete for a spot in the rotation.” Lynch will get that opportunity in spring training, but the Royals will have to weigh whether he’s better suited to the bullpen, where he has become a valuable weapon. Injured Luinder Avila showed some promise as a starter with good horizontal movement, but walks were an issue. He got hurt late in the year and had Tommy John surgery and will miss all of next season with the hope he can return in 2028. Ryan Bergert looked like a potential rotation candidate going into the 2026 season, but was shelved after just three minor league starts. He also had Tommy John surgery, but could be a candidate to return in the second half. Bergert gets strong strikeout numbers with a high-spin fastball and a slider with good break, but will need to keep the walks down. Stephen Kolek found success with the Royals with a very low walk rate and a lot of groundballs. He doesn’t miss many bats at all, but he shows good command and terrific pitch efficiency. He had Tommy John surgery late in the year and is unlikely to return at all in 2027. Ben Kudrna is a Kansas City native who ranked high on team prospect lists until he took a step back in the upper minors in 2025. After one minor league start this year, he had olecranon stress fracture surgery and missed the remainder of the season. He should return this year, but the team will likely slowly ease him back. He will turn 24 in January and if he returns to the high-strikeout pitcher he showed in the lower levels, he could be a factor. John Means is another local boy who had some success with the Orioles, earning an All-Star appearance in 2019. He has pitched in just ten big league games since 2021, missing time with two Tommy John surgeries. He ruptured his Achilles in 2025 as he attempted to come back, and returned to pitch in five minor league games for the Royals. The lefty is 33 years old now, but if he can stay healthy, he could be in the mix for a rotation spot. Cole Ragans has the highest upside of anyone on this list as an All-Star in 2024 who finished fourth in Cy Young voting. Over the last three seasons combined, only five starting pitchers in baseball with at least 200 innings pitched have a higher strikeout rate than his 31.3 percent. He made just eight starts this year before landing on the Injured List with a UCL injury that required surgery, although not Tommy John surgery. He could return in the second half of next year, and the Royals will need him to eventually get back to his All-Star level. Depth options Lucas Braun was acquired from Atlanta in the Lane Thomas trade at the deadline last summer. The 25-year-old right-hander finished 2026 with a 4.16 ERA and 120 strikeouts in 132 innings across Double-A and Triple-A. Braun doesn’t have overpowering stuff, with a fastball that sits around 92 mph, but he features a six-pitch mix and good command. He could compete for a rotation spot at some point in 2027, although he may need more seasoning at Omaha. Logan Evans came over in the Garcia trade after missing all of the 2026 season following surgery to repair a torn ulnar collateral ligament. He pitched in 16 games with the Mariners in 2025, with a 4.32 ERA and 59 strikeouts in 81.1 innings. He

item.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
item.description: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull , Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal ) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford . This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘He’s more elegant’: Bellingham downplays Zidane comparisons after wondergoal
item.description: Englishman hailed by teammates and manager Mourinho after coming on to completely change Champions League game against PSV Eindhoven “It was one of those moments when you’re just: ‘Wow.’” Bernardo Silva had a good view of Jude Bellingham scoring the goal, the golazo , that put Real Madrid into the lead and the Bernabéu on its feet, shock giving way to song, naa, naa, naa, na-na-na-naa, na-na-na-naa ringing round again. “I have no idea what I did,” the Englishman said afterwards. What he did was turn all Le Tissier. Lifting the ball with his left, raising it with his right, twisting and not letting it drop, he sent it arching from the outside of his boot into the far corner, something straight out of the 90s. “I just kind of hit it,” Bellingham reckoned; not wanting to hit it too hard, it had gone “looping”, “stabbing”, he said. “Normally [my goals are] a lot closer, aren’t they? I was a bit surprised, honestly. Normally from there I’m looking to see who is an option to play it through to, but it popped up nicely. It was nice.” Nice? It was, Silva said, “special”. A “work of art” Marca called it. The presenter on one radio station claimed it was the best goal he had ever seen, and it wasn’t just him; wasn’t just the goal, either. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Sid Lowe in Madrid
item.content:encoded: Englishman hailed by teammates and manager Mourinho after coming on to completely change Champions League game against PSV Eindhoven “It was one of those moments when you’re just: ‘Wow.’” Bernardo Silva had a good view of Jude Bellingham scoring the goal, the golazo , that put Real Madrid into the lead and the Bernabéu on its feet, shock giving way to song, naa, naa, naa, na-na-na-naa, na-na-na-naa ringing round again. “I have no idea what I did,” the Englishman said afterwards. What he did was turn all Le Tissier. Lifting the ball with his left, raising it with his right, twisting and not letting it drop, he sent it arching from the outside of his boot into the far corner, something straight out of the 90s. “I just kind of hit it,” Bellingham reckoned; not wanting to hit it too hard, it had gone “looping”, “stabbing”, he said. “Normally [my goals are] a lot closer, aren’t they? I was a bit surprised, honestly. Normally from there I’m looking to see who is an option to play it through to, but it popped up nicely. It was nice.” Nice? It was, Silva said, “special”. A “work of art” Marca called it. The presenter on one radio station claimed it was the best goal he had ever seen, and it wasn’t just him; wasn’t just the goal, either. Continue reading...

item.title: Senegal regaining Afcon title is the right end to embarrassing farrago but issues do not stop here | Osasu Obayiuwana
item.description: After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history. As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday , was a “big joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute. Continue reading...

item.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
item.description: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered. Continue reading...

item.title: Search for next USMNT head coach needs to prioritize competence over fame
item.description: The job of Mauricio Pochettino’s successor is to fine-tune a team on the up. That requires a bureaucrat rather than a figurehead First, let’s get the Pep Exception out of the way. Or perhaps we’d better call it the Guardiola Caveat. Regardless, the point is the same. If US Soccer can get Pep Guardiola to manage the United States men’s national team, it should. Because when you have the chance to employ the most successful and influential coach of his generation, the thinker who stands upstream of essentially every major tactical current of the last two decades, you just have to do it. But let us assume that US Soccer can’t appoint Guardiola, because he is only a few months into his post-Manchester City sabbatical and still busying himself defending his body of work . Because he has given no recent indication that he wants the job, even though he spent a previous break between managerial gigs living in New York City and was probably only being supportive of his newly-appointed colleague Mauricio Pochettino when he called the project “fascinating” two years ago. Also because he has only ever signed on to coach teams stacked with Ballon d’Or contenders, posing a Phil Jackson-type, bar-room question over whether he would still be exceptional in charge of unexceptional players. Then again, Guardiola says he expects his next job to be in international management, if and when he does return. Continue reading...

item.title: The story of how Pelé and Maradona went from friends to bitter rivals
item.description: A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979 Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, not long after the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to the finals of the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio. Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentine Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer. Continue reading...

item.title: Has a footballer had a longer career hiatus than Ronaldinho’s 11 year-gap? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the quickest team to go from FA Cup winners to the first round and matches delayed by snowball fights Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Ronaldinho played for Ravenna, in Serie C, earlier this month. It was his first professional appearance in more than 11 years,” writes George Jones. “Have any other footballers had long career hiatuses? And has any player had a longer hiatus than 11 years?” Ronaldinho’s last professional appearance before his return for Ravenna came on 26 September 2015 for Fluminense, who won 2-0 at home against Goiás. He was withdrawn after 45 minutes. Fans of symmetry will be pleased to see that 11 years and 50 days later, the Brazilian returned for Ravenna in a 2-0 home win against another team with five letters and an accent in their name, Forlì, and was withdrawn after 45 minutes. Continue reading...

item.title: Rayan Cherki magic denies Napoli but Manchester City’s struggles continue
item.description: For reasons best known to those eyeing the pound signs, Manchester City gave a debut to a special rust-coloured kit in front of a nonplussed crowd. It was of a piece with their performance for most of a familiarly frustrating night that at least concluded with a shot of energy, the home side belatedly shaking off their torpor and ending the prospect of a triumphant return to the Etihad for Kevin De Bruyne. Despite the relief sparked by a fine equaliser by Rayan Cherki, who was rewarded for an insistent but hitherto fruitless evening’s endeavours when his angled shot flashed past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, it was hard to see this as anything but a perfect snapshot of their autumn difficulties. Nobody could pretend City were up against crack opposition in a one-paced Napoli, who are eighth in Serie A and lack the brio of old, but they simply cannot keep the door shut and could not have quibbled about departing with a defeat. Continue reading...

item.title: Dortmund’s Beier halts Arsenal charge after thunderbolt from Gyökeres
item.description: Arsenal’s sky-high standards are slipping. For the second time in four days, Mikel Arteta’s side found themselves a goal up at half-time and apparently coasting toward victory, only for their opponents to rouse themselves and earn a deserved draw. After Newcastle on Saturday , this time it was an impressive Borussia Dortmund who became only the second side to take points off Arsenal in their past 15 group stage games in this competition. It could have been worse had an offside flag not ruled out Jobe ­Bellingham’s goal after Max Beier equalised a thunderbolt from Viktor Gyökeres. But the much-maligned Sweden striker was guilty of a glaring miss late on as Arsenal laid siege to Dortmund’s goal, racking up 30 shots by the final whistle. The German side had to hang on for a result that gave their travelling fans a night to remember, although Arteta admitted his players must be more clinical when Real Madrid and Jude Bellingham visit north London in a fortnight. Continue reading...

item.title: Gul takes pain for buoyant Galatasaray to condemn Aston Villa to Champions League loss
item.description: This was Aston Villa’s third trip to Istanbul in the calendar year but, this time, they departed with different emotions. Unlike on the banks of the Bosphorus at Besiktas Park in May, the scene of their unforgettable Europa League triumph , or at Fenerbahce in January, they came away with a bloody nose. Galatasaray’s match-winner, Deniz Gul, finished with similar, the substitute requiring a bandage after bravely taking a boot to the face from Nicolas Jackson as the hosts rippled the net on 77 minutes. It was the game’s first effort on target, Galatasaray maintaining their commanding form on home soil to extend Villa’s winless run to six matches in all competitions. On the outside, this is a gladiatorial arena, a giant spaceship parked on Ali Sami Yen complex. But inside there is a poor pitch that began cutting up during the warm-up. John McGinn, one of four changes from Villa’s stalemate with Sunderland on Saturday, gestured towards the turf in frustration after a through ball went awry, but nobody of a Villa persuasion could blame defeat on the surface. As Unai Emery had stated, it was the same for both teams. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | The game’s gone: has fantasy football been ruined by AI gafferbots?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Sometimes, the beautiful game can make Football Daily feel old. Even Monday’s ostensibly old-school fixture between Brentford and Everton felt like the future destroying the past. The analytics-coded hosts prevailed 4-0 and James Tarkowski was dismissed by the VAR overlords for a challenge that would have been considered “firm but fair” on the muddy pitches of our youth. “I don’t think you can tackle like that in this day and age,” a misty-eyed David Moyes sighed after the game, before heading to the team bus to rewatch the Battle of Santiago . If Sunday was Gary Neville’s Sistine Chapel [ Monday’s Football Daily ], then his commentary on the Fernando Torres goal for Chelsea against Barcelona must be his David ” – Ronnie McMahon. Regarding Declan Hackett’s assertion [ Monday’s letters ] that Donald Trump will be helping his mate Mauricio Pochettino by ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card, perhaps Poch should be careful what he wishes for: Trump may equally decide to get Michael Carrick reinstated, as he also has a bit of previous for that sort of thing” – Dexter O Riordan. In all the time that I have been watching football, I don’t think I have ever seen a player dismiss himself and be away down the tunnel before given a red card. Thanks James Tarkowski ” – Nigel Sanders. Brighton had only failed to win twice in the league since 5 September. A 1-1 draw with Leeds and a 2-0 defeat at Liverpool - their only opponents with double letters in their name. That bizarre hoodoo struck again at Hull on Sunday. Good good news for Seagulls fans is the only double-lettered encounters they have before hosting Hull in February are trips to Forest and Spurs. Even better news is that since that 1-1 draw with Leeds on 5 September, they have a 100% win record against sides without double letters and have not conceded a goal” – Dan Ashley (and no others). Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I’m loving it at Brugge’: Freddie Potts on going from West Ham’s bench to Champions League
item.description: Midfielder is preparing to face Liverpool after leaving the club he loves and overcoming a tough start in Belgium In April Freddie Potts was absorbing the disappointment of being substituted at half-time during West Ham’s FA Cup quarter-final defeat by Leeds. The midfielder was out of favour under Nuno Espírito Santo and could not have imagined that he would be preparing to face Liverpool in the Champions League seven months later. It is the 23-year-old’s reward for taking the difficult decision to leave his boyhood club last summer. Potts noticed his minutes were drying up in pre-season, even though West Ham were not exactly stocked with talent after relegation, and he was ready for a new challenge when Club Brugge offered about £10m to sign him. The midfielder was out of favour under Nuno Espírito Santo and could not have imagined that he would be preparing to face Liverpool in the Champions League seven months later. It is the 23-year-old’s reward for taking the difficult decision to leave his boyhood club last summer. Potts noticed his minutes were drying up in pre-season, even though West Ham were not exactly stocked with talent after relegation, and he was ready for a new challenge when Club Brugge offered about £10m to sign him. item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Neville, Keane and Manchester United meltdowns at world’s funniest comedy club
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Hoo-boy. Short of forgetting to put on his washable virgin wool navy trousers before striding towards the visitors’ dugout at Anfield, it’s difficult to imagine how Mauricio Pochettino’s spell in charge of Manchester United could have got off to a more humiliating start. Having witnessed his new team go a man and two goals down in less time than it takes to listen to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven twice, it was a rendition of Sacked In The Morning that could be heard from the home fans inside 15 minutes. Poch would later complain that the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro was questionable, but it was far less baffling than his own call to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in a year after almost 12 months out with knack. Across 90 harrowing minutes, the Dutch defender didn’t so much look off the pace as resemble a confused tourist who’d wandered on to the pitch while trying to find his way to the stadium museum. In a footballing world obsessed with micro-marginal-gains – think custom-weighted laces, aerodynamic socks, or nice calming shades of green for training ground walls – how about one modest proposal that otherwise does my nut in? That a multimillion pound player, paid hundred of thousands each week, has to walk all the way around the pitch with ligament injuries . Carry him, give him crutches, or put him in a wheelchair! Is it just me? It has a very 1950s amateur air of ‘dont make a fuss, ‘tis a mere scratch’” – John Williams. Since he was such a good friend to Mauricio Pochettino in his previous role, can we assume Donald Trump will be ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card once he’s finished his morning nap?” – Declan Hackett. If Mikel Arteta is correct in his assertion that “ We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League ” how does he explain his team’s Micky Mouse defending for Newcastle’s second goal at St James’ Park on Sunday?” – Dominic Hodgson. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: PSG had the best attack in Europe but Doué and Kvaratskhelia injuries will test Luis Enrique
item.description: Désiré Doué sustained an ACL injury in PSG’s 3-2 win at Nice and joins Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the treatment table By Get French Football News Luis Enrique is in uncharted territory, even if he insists that “it isn’t a first”. Since arriving at Paris Saint-Germain in 2023, only three players have spent more than 100 days on the sideline – Nuno Mendes, Lucas Hernandez and Presnel Kimpembe – and only Mendes is an important first-team player. But for the remainder of the season, or at least the vast majority of it, Luis Enrique must do without two of his stars: Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. Doué arrived in Nice on Saturday evening already bearing scars. The PSG forward wore a mouth guard after Davide Frattesi had dislodged one of his front teeth with a stray arm during France’s defeat by Italy during the international break. Continue reading...

item.title: Esposito emulates Vieri with Inter hat-trick but De Ketelaere haunts him again
item.description: Italy’s new cover star enjoyed a ‘beautiful’ treble but could not celebrate it after his side threw away two-goal leads three times to draw 4-4 with Atalanta This ought to have been a magic moment for Pio Esposito. He had just scored his first Serie A hat-trick, becoming only the third Italian to get one for Inter in the era of three points for a win. The last to do it was Christian Vieri, back in 2003. Two years before Esposito was born. We will come back to that. Esposito has been drawing premature comparisons to Vieri for some time and especially now after a barnstorming November in which he has scored eight times in five games, including three in two for his country, and two of those as part of a man-of-the-match performance during an upset win against France . Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson Match report: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision Continue reading...

item.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
item.description: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot. It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will. Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...
